World.title: Police join protest victims' Sh25.75m reparations payout
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Prof. Makau Mutua, Chairperson of the Panel of Experts on Compensation of Victims of Human Rights Violations. [File,Standard]

A protest reparations panel has approved compensation for 49 police officers, awarding them Sh25.75 million alongside payments to civilians who suffered human rights violations.

The Panel of Experts on Compensation of Victims of Human Rights Violations approved seven claims involving severe injuries, 37 for moderate injuries and five for minor injuries, according to an update issued Friday, August 7.

"In acknowledgement of the dedication by our uniformed officers to protecting the public, the Panel has resolved to grant appropriate compensation for the human rights violations they sustained during the period in question," the panel said.

The inclusion of police officers adds a new dimension to a compensation programme created against the backdrop of protests in which police conduct has faced scrutiny.

During protests between June 17 and July 7, 2025, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA) recorded 65 deaths, 342 civilian injuries and 171 injuries to police officers.

IPOA said most of the deaths were linked mainly to police actions during crowd-control operations.

The compensation programme grew out of the National Dialogue Committee (NADCO) process, which sought to address political and governance tensions in Kenya.

The government later set aside Sh2 billion for victims of human rights violations linked to protests and other demonstrations between 2017 and 2025.

The panel reported that it has processed 680 claims and disbursed Sh896.1 million in compensation.

The panel listed three phases of payments as Sh448.7 million in the initial phase, Sh225.4 million in the second phase and Sh247.95 million in the third phase.

The latest phase covered 175 civilian victims and included 50 fatalities, 46 severe injuries, 49 moderate injuries, 21 minor injuries and nine economic-loss claims.

The panel reported total payments of Sh222 million for the phase.

However, 472 claims submitted through IPOA and KNCHR remain outstanding because applicants have not provided enough supporting documents.

The panel is working with IPOA regional offices to locate affected victims and their beneficiaries and obtain the documents required to process the claims.

The backlog includes 594 of the 600 economic-loss claims received by the panel. Only four have been processed and compensated.

The panel has also received nine claims under the sexual offences category. Eight have been processed and compensated while one remains pending.

Claims involving enforced disappearances remain under review because the panel says the cases require investigation and verification before they can be approved, referred for further investigation or declared ineligible.

The panel has also reclassified three claims from minor to severe after reviewing medical reports and additional submissions.

It approved above-scale compensation for five victims whose injuries it described as permanent and life-altering and said it would recommend that President Ruto include them in a government-funded lifetime medical scheme.

World.title: EACC arrests Kitui County Chief Officer over Sh17.48m procurement fraud
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kitui County Chief Officer Gladys Mami Kivoto and five company directors arrested by EACC. [Joh Muia, Standard]

The Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) has arrested Kitui County Chief Officer Gladys Mami Kivoto and five company directors over alleged conflict of interest and procurement irregularities involving Sh17.48 million contracts.

In a statement on Thursday, EACC CEO Abdi Mohamud said investigations found that Kivoto, who served in the Departments of Agriculture & Fisheries and Irrigation, allegedly traded with the county through five proxy companies: Shanel Construction Ltd, ECO Stone Ltd, AZ Links Ltd, DTK Construction Ltd, and 4-Walls Ltd.

The companies were paid a total of Sh14.1 million by the county between the 2018/2019 and 2024/2025 financial years.

EACC further established that three of the directors, Josephine Mwikali Wambua of Shanel Construction, Makoma Wambua of AZ Links and Emmanuel Wambua of ECO Stone are relatives of Kivoto. There were also financial transactions between Kivoto and directors of DTK Construction and 4-Walls.

Following investigations, the file was forwarded to the DPP, who approved charges against nine suspects, including conflict of interest, abuse of office, money laundering, and corrupt procurement.

Those arrested are Gladys Mami Kivoto, Josephine Mwikali Wambua Director, Shanel Construction, Roselyne Kyambi Kilonzi Director, Shanel Construction, Mary Mueni Mbiti Director, DTK Construction & 4-Walls, Jonathan Kivondo Kieti Director, DTK Construction and Onesmus Munyao Nzioka Director, ECO Stone.

EACC directed Makoma Wambua of ECO Stone, Emmanuel Wambua of AZ Links, and Stella Nthenya Kioko of AZ Links who are reportedly in hiding to present themselves at the EACC Lower Eastern Regional Office in Machakos or the nearest EACC office for processing.

The suspects are expected to be arraigned at the Kitui Law Courts.

World.title: High Court orders striking nurses back to work
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Uasin Gishu County nurses strike over delayed payments and unfulfilled Collective Bargaining Agreement [Wycliff Kipsang, Standard]

Nurses across the 47 counties have been ordered to report back to work immediately or face legal action from the counties.

Justice Monica Mbaru of the Employment and Labour Court in Mombasa issued orders temporarily stopping the nationwide nurse strike that commenced on July 29, 2026, and ordered the Kenya National Union of Nurses and Midwives (KNUNM) to direct its members back to work.

Justice Mbaru said on Wednesday that any nurse absent from work without proper and lawful cause shall face disciplinary action.

This is after Mombasa County Government and its Public Service Board successfully enjoined the 46 county governments to make the order national.

“In the interim, the KNUNM (respondent) is hereby restrained from undertaking any industrial action relating to the strike notices dated July 21 and July 29 and shall direct all its members to resume duty forthwith and unconditionally to allow the court to address the claim herein on a priority basis,” said Justice Mbaru.

The judge ordered all county labour officers in the 47 counties to record attendance of nurses who report to work and compile a report in court on September 22, 2026.

“Any member of the KNUNM who will be noted by the County Labour Officer as absent from duty without lawful cause shall allow the counties to issue necessary notice to show cause why disciplinary action should not be taken,” said Justice Mbaru.

In their petition certified urgent, Mombasa County claimed that the nurses strike has crippled services in public hospitals across all the 47 counties, thereby placing patients facing emergency and inpatient care at risk.

In Mombasa County, the nurses strike paralysed medical services at all medical facilities, including Coast General Hospital, Port Reitz Hospital, Likoni District Hospital and Shimo La Tewa GK Prison Hospital.

Mombasa County, through its Counsel Murtaza Tajbhai, said that the strike had turned from a labour disagreement to a matter of immense public interest.

Tajbhai said that the nurses’ union proceeded with the said strike despite the Mombasa Public Service Board inviting the KNUNM officials for talks to avert the said strike.

The union had raised concerns over the 2025-2029 Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA), implementation of the 2017 Return to Work Formula and pension terms for Universal Health Coverage staff care guidelines for nurses and the reinstatement of 46 nurses dismissed in Kisii County.

However, in their petition, Mombasa County said that the said grievances could not be addressed by each county individually.

Mombasa County Service Board Chief Executive Officer Fadhil Maamum told the court in his affidavit that most of the demands required consultation with national institutions like the Salaries and Remuneration Commission, while others cannot be implemented immediately given their significant financial implications.

He said that nurses under Mombasa County have no salary arrears and had met some of the union’s demands through negotiations.

Maamum said that while the nurses’ grievances can be resolved, the patients do not have the luxury of time.

“Nurses are designated essential service providers under the Labour Relations Act and the industrial action was unlawful because the statutory dispute resolution mechanism had not been exhausted," said Maamum.

He said the court's intervention will allow for negotiations and safeguard the constitutional right to healthcare.

However, the Union said that the strike was after failed action by the counties to meet their agreed grievances despite continued negotiations.

The nurses said they will not be reporting to work unless guided by the union.

World.title: NTSA blamed for poor signage, costly penalties
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

A temporary speed signage on Likoni Road, Nairobi. [Screengrab]

A growing number of motorists are raising concerns about fines issued by the National Transport and Safety Authority's (NTSA) automated speed camera system, claiming they are being penalised without sufficient warning, transparency, or an opportunity to challenge the alleged offences.

The complaints come after the government rolled out a nationwide network of smart traffic cameras aimed at curbing speeding and reducing road carnage.

The cameras automatically detect speeding vehicles, identify registration numbers and generate instant penalties, with notifications sent to registered vehicle owners via SMS.

While authorities have hailed the technology as a game-changer in road safety, many drivers say the system has become a source of frustration and financial burden.

Some motorists claim they have received multiple speeding fines within a single journey, while others argue they were penalised despite maintaining the posted speed limits.

In some places, motorists argue that most signs are on one side of the road, even though the road is a dual carriageway, making it difficult for most road users.

Several have questioned the accuracy of the cameras, citing cases where they were allegedly fined long after travelling through the affected roads.

The debate has been raging on social media, with the latest complaint being on the speed signage along Likoni Road, Nairobi, where motorists are mandated to drive at 30km/h.

"NTSA can't be the complainant, regulator, enforcer, prosecutor, Jury, judge, and collector all-in-one. They could be chasing internal collection targets, while hurting the common man,"

Others have expressed concern over the placement of some speed cameras, saying they are positioned in areas where speed limit signs are either unclear, obscured or insufficient.

"They fined me near Industrial Park Eastern Bypass where on that entire stretch there is no sign indicating the speed limit. This is a shakedown; someone is minting this money," a user on X lamented.

According to the drivers, this leaves road users vulnerable to inadvertent violations.

"There is no problem with enforcing traffic laws, but motorists deserve clear signage, accurate records and a fair opportunity to dispute fines they believe were issued in error," said one driver who recently received multiple speed notifications along the Northern Bypass.

The automated enforcement system forms part of NTSA's broader road safety reforms under the Minor Traffic Offences Framework, which allows specified offences to be handled administratively instead of through the courts.

NTSA says the initiative is intended to eliminate corruption associated with roadside enforcement, improve compliance with traffic laws and reduce the backlog of traffic cases in courts.

Under the framework, speeding attracts graduated penalties depending on how far a driver exceeds the prescribed limit.

Minor violations may attract warnings or lower fines, while more serious offences carry significantly higher penalties.

The automated fines programme also faced an earlier legal challenge after petitioners argued that motorists were being punished without adequate due process.

The dispute centred on whether automated enforcement infringed constitutional rights to fair administrative action and a fair hearing before penalties are imposed.

Road safety experts, however, maintain that excessive speed remains one of the leading causes of fatal crashes in Kenya and argue that consistent, technology-driven enforcement is more effective than sporadic roadside operations.

They contend that unlike manual enforcement, automated cameras minimise opportunities for bribery and apply traffic laws uniformly to all motorists.

Even so, transport stakeholders are urging NTSA to improve public awareness, ensure speed limit signs are visible and regularly calibrated, and establish an efficient appeals mechanism for motorists who believe they have been wrongly fined.

According to Volume 6 on Traffic Control Facilities and the Traffic Signs Manual, the Ministry of Transport is mandated to ensure the speed limit sign boards are erected above pedestrian footways with a minimum clearance of 2.2m from the bottom of the sign to the pavement.

At the same time, the signs should be placed at an absolute minimum horizontal clearance of 0.5 m from the outer edge of the usable shoulder or carriageway.

World.title: Mukurweini MP John Kaguchia arraigned over alleged inciting remarks
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Mukurweini MP John Kaguchia arrives at the Milimani Law Courts in Nairobi on August 4, 2026. [Nancy Gitonga, Standard]

Mukurweini MP John Kaguchia was on Tuesday arraigned before the Milimani Law Courts over alleged inciting remarks made during a political rally in Kieni, Nyeri County.

Appearing before Senior Principal Magistrate Teresia Nyangena, Kaguchia was read the charge of offensive conduct by the court clerk but did not respond after his lawyers mounted a spirited constitutional challenge against the charges.

His legal team objected to the manner in which the charges had been framed, arguing they violated several constitutional safeguards and should not proceed.

The courtroom was packed to capacity as a battery of lawyers appeared for the legislator alongside political allies who turned up in solidarity.

Among those present were Nyeri Senator John Methu, Nyeri Woman Representative Jane Njeri Maina and several elected leaders who followed the proceedings from the public gallery.

The defence argued that the charge sheet failed to meet the constitutional threshold set under Article 50(2) which guarantees every accused person the right to be informed of the charge with sufficient detail to answer it.

The charge before you does not disclose an offence under the law and purely an attempt by the state to breach the freedom of expression and limiting the opposition.

Lead defence counsel Kiragu Wathuta and Ndegwa Njiru told the court that the MP's constitutional rights had been violated from the time of his arrest.

The lawyers narrated that on the night of August 2, Kaguchia had appeared on Inooro FM's Kiririmbi programme where public affairs were being discussed between 7 pm. and 9 pm.

According to the lawyer, after the programme ended, staff at the Royal Media Services station allegedly informed the MP that about 30 Subaru vehicles carrying hooded individuals had surrounded the premises looking for him.

"Because of the wave of abductions in this country, I advised him to remain within the Royal Media Services premises. At about 5 a.m., I found him having spent the night on the station's couches waiting for daylight," lawyer told the court.

He said that at around 9 a.m., a senior officer who identified himself as a regional DCI commander arrived with uniformed officers and informed the MP that he was under arrest despite there being no summons or warrant issued against him.

"When we inquired why no summons had been issued as is the normal procedure, the investigating officer told us they were acting on instructions from above," the lawuer submitted.

The lawyer further claimed officers initially indicated Kaguchia would be taken to Kilimani before driving him instead to DCI headquarters, where he said advocates were denied access to their client.

"They told us no counsel would be allowed into the DCI premises. Lawyers were locked out and denied an opportunity to consult with the accused," he said.

According to the defence, lawyers later moved to court and obtained orders from Kiambu High Court granting Kaguchia police bail of Sh100,000.

However, they alleged officers at Kamukunji Police Station refused to process the release despite the cash bail being available.

The lawyer told the court that the Officer Commanding Station allegedly declined to accept the money, saying he had received instructions that the legislator could not be released from the station and should instead deposit the cash bail at Central Police Station.

"The accused is not before this court because of any crime he committed. He is here to demonstrate to the country that it is now a crime to oppose the government," he argued.

Lawyer Wathuta also informed the court that Justice Gregory Mutai had on Tuesday morning in Milimani High Court Human Rights Petition No. E517 of 2026 granted the MP a bond of Sh500,000 and directed police to facilitate his access to legal counsel.

Lawyer Ndegwa Njiru argued that Kaguchia could not be required to plead before first receiving legal advice, citing Article 49(1)(c) of the Constitution, which guarantees every arrested person the right to communicate with and be represented by an advocate.

Njiru further challenged the jurisdiction of the Milimani court, arguing that the alleged offence was said to have occurred in Kieni, Nyeri County, and should therefore be prosecuted before a court with territorial jurisdiction over the alleged incident.

He also argued that the charge under Section 94(1) of the Penal Code was defective because it did not disclose who had allegedly been threatened, abused or insulted.

"The charge sheet merely refers to words allegedly uttered by the accused but fails to demonstrate that they were made in a public place or that they amounted to threatening, abusive or insulting words as required by law," Njiru submitted.

He also questioned the accuracy of the translated charge sheet, telling the court he understood Kikuyu and had noticed discrepancies between the original alleged utterances and the English translation.

Njiru argued that the translation distorted the alleged remarks, particularly the reference to the word "Kasongo", and maintained that the inconsistencies prejudiced the accused's ability to understand the charge.

He further submitted that the offence under Section 94 of the Penal Code is a misdemeanour punishable by a maximum sentence of six months imprisonment or a fine not exceeding Sh5,000.

Njiru argued that under Article 49(2) of the Constitution, Kaguchia ought not to have remained in custody for two nights over such an offence.

The defence also urged the court to order the release of the MP's Samsung A33 mobile phone, arguing that it had no connection to the alleged offence.

The hearing on the preliminary objections is still ongoing before Milimani Law Courts

World.title: Tension at Kamukunji Police Station as leaders demand Kaguchia's release
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Mukuruwe-ini MP John Kaguchia at Kamukunji Police Station in Nairobi on August 3, 2026. [Collins Oduor, Standard]

Tension is high at Kamukunji Police Station as opposition leaders led by Kipipiri MP Wanjiku Muhia and lawyers demand the immediate release of Mukurweini MP John Kaguchia, claiming police had failed to comply with a High Court order granting him police cash bail.

Kaguchia, who was arrested earlier on Monday over alleged electoral offences and incitement, remained in police custody hours after his lawyers said the court had ordered his release on Sh100,000 police bail.

Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua in a post on his Facebook account said that the High Court had issued orders directing the Officer Commanding Station (OCS) at Kamukunji Police Station to release the legislator immediately upon payment of the bail.

Gachagua said that despite the court order having been served, the OCS had not acted and was instead awaiting instructions from his superiors. He warned the officer against disobeying a court order, saying that he could be held personally liable for contempt of court if the directive was ignored.

The former Deputy President further referenced the ongoing murder case involving the former OCS of Central Police Station, urging police officers to uphold the law and avoid carrying out unlawful instructions.

Several Members of Parliament from the Mt Kenya region have camped outside Kamukunji Police Station, insisting they would not leave until Kaguchia is released. The legislators accused police of delaying compliance with the court order and questioned why the MP was still being held despite the court's directive.

The lawmakers that claimed they had been redirected to Central Police Station while seeking information about Kaguchia's detention.

Kaguchia's arrest has sparked political debate, with opposition leaders accusing investigative agencies of selectively enforcing the law against government critics. They argue that other leaders who have previously made controversial public statements have not faced similar action.

World.title: Why Kenyans' trust gap on IEBC continues to grow
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

IEBC is gaining mistrust among Kenyans. [File, Standard]

The reconstituted Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) assumed office about a year ago on the backdrop of growing mistrust among Kenyans.

But, even before it conducts its first General Elections, the Commission is already confronting a fresh credibility test after proposing restrictions on the livestreaming of election results.

The proposal, presented as part of efforts to safeguard the integrity of the tallying process, has instead reignited long-standing public anxieties over transparency in the country's electoral management system.

For many Kenyans, whose confidence in election management has been repeatedly shaken by disputed presidential results, court battles and allegations of manipulation, the move has reinforced fears that access to real-time information could be curtailed at the most critical stage of the democratic process.

The government sponsored Bill, whose fate now lies with the National Assembly, is jointly sponsored by Senate Majority leader Aaron Cheruiyot and Minority leader Stewart Madzayo.

The Bill that has stalled at the First Reading level in the Assembly since February 2024, seeks to repeal section 39(1)(g) of the Elections Act.

If approved, live transmission of results displayed by the Commission at the National Tallying Centre may not be there in the 2027 polls.

Kenyans have since responded to the proposal, pouring their anger and outrage as they question the motive behind the proposal, with some suggesting that the move could be introduced to conceal ill motives during elections.

"No doubt this is exactly what the IEBC fears; a transparent electoral process that every Kenyan can verify,' Wabowoba Calwo said on X in a post accompanied by a clip where an individual is seen pointing at a screen livestreaming the recently conducted Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election.

"Kenyans must demand nothing less than a free and fair 2027 election," he added, asserting that "transparency is not going to be a favour by anybody, it is a democratic safeguard."

According to another user, banning of real-time live streaming of election results would undermine the integrity of polls and create anxiety among voters.

"If the IEBC fails to livestream the General Election, it will create unnecessary suspicion, undermine transparency and provide fertile ground for claims of electoral malpractice," he posted.

According to Yamine, an X user, live broadcasts of election results keep Kenyans informed. promote transparency, provide a clear picture of the voting process, and help ease tension rather than "fuel uncertainty."

"In real democracies, results are streamed live so every citizen can watch and decide for themselves," posted Yamine.

Alfred Abuya said :"I strongly reject this move. Why will they even imagine doing something like counting votes in the dark? Are they working for someone or independent forces behind the idea?"

However, IEBC has since denied claims that the proposed law seeks to scrap the live transmission of election results, saying they have been misunderstood.

In a statement on Thursday, the Commission said the Bill does not amend Section 44 of the Elections Act, which provides for the Integrated Elections Management System used for Voter registration.

It argued, instead, that the amendment is envisioned to introduce an alternative transmission mechanism for areas without the minimum 3G network required to electronically transmit results.

The Commission further said it will still be required to verify results by comparing the original physical Form 34A with its electronically submitted results.

"The Bill seeks to align the law with the Supreme Court's decision in Presidential Election Petition No 1 of 20217, which affirmed that the election result is one recorded in the statutory Results Declaration Form (Form 34A Series), the primary and final record of the results at the polling station," said the commission.

According to youth activist Allans Ademba who mobilised the "Tuko Kadi" mass voter registration call, the move will erode public trust in the agency.

"If IEBC wants to win the trust of youths, it must ensure credible results. This can only happen if they allow live streaming," he said, adding that "apart from malicious forms which the commission can manage, there was no need to ban it."

Appearing on a local TV show early this week, nominated MP Sabina Chege, said the electoral agency was yet to justify to Kenyans what informed such a decision.

"The IEBC has not provided any justification for mending the live streaming of elections," she said.

Former National Assembly Speaker Justin Muturi has also criticised the proposal, terming it retrogressive and an outright attack on democracy and the rule of law.

"Any proposal from whichever quarter to ban the live streaming of election results is not only unconstitutional and offensive to the principles of open governance, but also a stain on the democratic conscience of the Kenyan people," he said.

He said "Darkness and democracy are not synonymous. Transparency is the life -blood of free, fair and credible elections."

Appearing on Spice Fm morning show on Thursday, Lawyer Ndegwa Njiru said: "Our Constitution is built on the principles of transparency, accountability and the participation of the people. Election results are not the property of the IEBC, they belong to Kenyans.

World.title: Al-Teatro
World.content:
From the land of Egypt and the stage of El Salam Theater came an unforgettable experience watching the play “Al-Teatro.” It offered two hours of pure visual and auditory delight—spanning set design, songs, acting performances, and a compelling message. In short, I was fortunate to enjoy a purposeful, highly entertaining production that excelled across every theatrical dimension.

I will not deconstruct or analyze every individual element of “Al-Teatro” here, as each component truly deserves an article of its own. Instead, I want to highlight the director, Ahmed Fouad—a maestro who conducted his theatrical symphony with outstanding directorial mastery. His artistic vision gave every single element its due space, seamlessly integrating dramatic technique and stage presentation.

The play unfolded like a harmonious musical composition, rich in thought, performance, and directorial craft that left the audience completely immersed in the true essence of theater. It was a feeling we had sorely missed, and “Al-Teatro” brought back those beautiful, authentic meanings of what theater should be.

The director skillfully leaned into the core theme: “Give me a theatre, and I will give you a civilization.” his is the kind of theater we grew up with and read so much about—where the civilization and history of any nation are born from its culture and dramatic arts.

Theater is the mother of all arts, a mirror reflecting a country’s identity. That remains the driving theme of “Al-Teatro,” which demonstrates that no matter how tastes, conflicts, conditions, or social classes evolve, genuine talent and refined art always triumph across the ages.

As mentioned at the outset, this piece is not a formal breakdown or critique. Rather, these lines serve as a message of gratitude to all those responsible in the Arab Republic of Egypt, led by the Egyptian Ministry of Culture, for supporting Egyptian and Arab culture so that Egypt remains the beacon of Arab culture and the pioneer of Arab theater.

Thank you to the entire cast and crew of “Al-Teatro,” and special thanks to director Ahmed Fouad for this exceptional show—specifically for championing young talent, blending their energy with established heavyweights of Egyptian and Arab theater through a distinct directorial vision.

Author’s biography

Nermin al-Houti is an associate professor of the Department of Criticism at the Higher Institute of Dramatic Arts in Kuwait.

She holds a PhD in Philosophy of Literary Criticism and is a graduate of the Higher Institute of Dramatic Arts.

Houti is a member of the Association of Writers and the Journalists Association, and is also part of the literary arbitration committees on theater or poetry in Kuwait and other Arab countries.

She has authored numerous newspapers and magazines articles and several books on significant theatrical works examining women’s issues, the latest of which is “The Women in Ismail Abdullah’s Theater”.

She has been chosen as a panelist in various significant cultural events and has participated in multiple seminars across the Arab region.

World.title: Mohamed Salah offered unusual gift in Turkey
World.content:
During a recent visit to the Araklı district in Trabzon, local Mayor Hüseyin Avni Coşkun Çebi shared a lighthearted moment with Egyptian football icon Mohamed Salah, offering him a parcel of land in the area following his high-profile transfer to Trabzonspor.

Leveraging Araklı’s favorable environmental outlook, the mayor jokingly pitched the district as an ideal retreat from global warming, telling the Egyptian captain: “Let us gift you a beautiful piece of land in a stunning location that is geographically secure from future climate change impact.”

The Mayor’s humorous gesture subtly referenced Egypt’s rising summer temperatures and broader climate challenges. Salah met the unique offer with a warm smile, leaving the invitation unanswered as the visit concluded in a friendly, high-energy atmosphere.

Footage and photos of the interaction quickly went viral across Turkish media and social platforms, with fans celebrating the mayor’s humor as a sign of the warm hospitality welcoming the Liverpool legend to the Black Sea region.

Salah completed a landmark move to Turkish Super Lig club Trabzonspor, triggering immense excitement across the city. Trabzon, situated along Turkey’s northern Black Sea coast, is renowned for its lush greenery, cooler maritime climate, and passionate football culture.

World.title: Egypt targets record-breaking 20+ million tourists in 2026
World.content:
Egypt’s tourism sector is poised to shatter records in 2026, with projections indicating international arrivals will exceed 20 million visitors. Fueled by booming demand from Arab and Gulf markets, extensive airport expansions, and growing hotel capacity, the country continues to strengthen its position as a top global destination.

The Arab market stands out as a primary driver of this growth. Tourist arrivals from Gulf nations and Jordan have recorded a notable surge during the current season, reflecting rising demand for coastal and cultural destinations—most notably New Alamein City, which continues to draw growing numbers of Arab visitors.

In this context, Hamdi Ezz, Head of the Tourism Syndicate, confirmed that the Arab market has become a core pillar of growth for Egypt’s tourism sector. He projected that total tourist arrivals to Egypt will cross the 20-million mark by the end of 2026, supported by political and security stability, infrastructure upgrades, and rising sectoral investments.

Ezz stated that Egypt welcomed approximately 19 million tourists in 2025—a 21% growth rate compared to the previous year. He noted that indicators for the current season reflect sustained momentum, backed by political and security stability, expanding infrastructure projects, and upgraded hospitality services.

He added that New Alamein City has emerged as one of the premier Arab summer destinations after achieving an extraordinary 450% growth in charter flight traffic, hosting visitors from 104 nationalities led by delegations from Gulf countries—reflecting the city’s success in cementing its place on the regional tourism map.

The Syndicate Head highlighted that airport development serves as a fundamental pillar to accommodate expected growth in tourist traffic, noting that the state aims to raise total airport capacity to 72.2 million passengers annually during the 2026/2027 fiscal year, up from 66.2 million passengers currently. This comes alongside ongoing operational modernizations, including Cairo International Airport renewing its Integrated Management System (ISO) certifications for 2026 in line with international standards.

Regarding the hotel sector, Ezz explained that Egypt is preparing to add roughly 7,000 new hotel rooms this year, including 3,445 rooms in Greater Cairo, alongside massive private tourism investments—most notably Travco Group’s plan to inject $1.5 billion to build 10 new hotels, helping meet rising demand for Egyptian destinations.

Ezz emphasized that Arab tourists now view Egypt as an all-inclusive destination offering natural assets, rich heritage, high service quality, and warm hospitality, stressing that current growth represents “not merely an increase in numbers, but a genuine shift in Egypt’s tourism standing, establishing a new phase of partnership with Arab markets.”

He added: “In recent years, the Arab market has proven to be a strategic partner for Egypt’s tourism sector. With ongoing airport upgrades, expanding hotel capacity, and the emergence of new destinations like New Alamein, we expect growth rates to continue and state targets of reaching over 20 million tourists to be met, while strengthening tourism’s contribution to the national economy.”

Dr. Magdy Sadek, a member of the Chamber of Travel and Tourism Agencies, stated that Egypt is currently witnessing high demand from Arab tourists, noting that various tourist destinations—led by the North Coast, Hurghada, Sharm El-Sheikh, and Alexandria—are welcoming growing numbers of visitors from Arab nations.

In exclusive statements to Al-Masry Al-Youm, Sadek added that the Egyptian destination has become the preferred choice for Arab tourists, not only for its beaches, resorts, and diverse tourist assets, but also for the sense of familiarity and cultural closeness visitors feel. He noted that Arab visitors view Egypt as an extension of their own environment, finding a welcome and hospitality that makes them feel right at home.

Sadek explained that declining interest in some competing destinations has contributed to increased arrivals in Egypt, emphasizing that Arab tourists seek destinations that offer safety and stability alongside high service quality—qualities Egypt has successfully established in recent years.

He pointed out that challenging weather conditions in parts of the region, along with regional tensions, have prompted many Arab families to extend their stays in Egypt. He explained that many do not come merely for short vacations, but prefer longer stays due to the stability and favorable atmosphere the country provides.

The Chamber of Travel and Tourism Agencies member affirmed that Egypt was and will remain the closest destination to its Arab brothers, given its historical and cultural standing, as well as its continuous keenness to welcome visitors from across the Arab world by offering a tourist experience combining safety, hospitality, and a diversity of destinations.

World.title: Which Egyptian star just joined the ranks of Africa’s most expensive footballers?
World.content:
Egyptian forward Omar Marmoush has cemented his status as one of Africa’s most elite football talents, ranking among the top four most expensive African players in history following his landmark $87 million transfer from Eintracht Frankfurt to English Premier League giants Manchester City.

Marmoush’s stellar performance in Europe paved the way for his mega-money move to Manchester, making him the most expensive Egyptian player in history and putting Arab talent firmly in the global transfer spotlight alongside North African stars Achraf Hakimi and Riyad Mahrez.

The list of Africa’s most lucrative transfers was recently reshaped by Ivorian winger Yan Diomande, whose historic $144 million move from RB Leipzig to Real Madrid set a new record as the most expensive African transfer of all time. Diomande surpassed the long-standing record held by his compatriot Nicolas Pépé ($92 million to Arsenal) and Nigerian striker Victor Osimhen ($91 million to Napoli).

The top 10 most expensive African footballers of all time

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises amid growing Middle East uncertainty
World.content:
The US dollar edged higher on Friday, against both the Japanese yen and the euro, extending gains from the previous session as growing doubts over reaching a peace deal with Iran bolstered the greenback’s safe-haven appeal.

The dollar also gained additional support from rising US Treasury yields following a Financial Times report, which cited sources close to Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh hinting at the possibility of an interest rate hike in September, depending on upcoming economic data.

During Asian trading early Friday morning, the US dollar rose to 158.505 yen after posting a 0.4 percent gain on Thursday, putting it on track for a weekly gain of approximately 0.7 percent.

This comes after rebounding from a sharp drop triggered by a joint intervention by Japan and the United States in the foreign exchange market, which had pushed the dollar down from a near four-decade high of over 163 yen to a 13-week low of 155.20 yen on Monday.

Against the euro today, the dollar posted modest gains, trading at $1.1521 per euro after advancing roughly 0.3 percent in the prior session.

According to Reuters data, the dollar also recorded a slight gain against the British pound, rising to $1.3449.

Conversely, the Australian dollar saw a minor decline to $0.7029, while the New Zealand dollar dropped slightly to $0.5866.

World.title: Cairo Airport enters the AI era with new 70-million-passenger terminal 4 expansion
World.content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) and digital transformation are taking the center stage in Cairo International Airport’s new Terminal IV project, designed to deliver a smart, highly efficient passenger experience.

During a meeting led by Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly in New Alamein City to review the project’s progress, Civil Aviation Minister Sameh al-Hefny highlighted that Terminal IV will leverage AI to streamline airport operations while maintaining high environmental sustainability standards.

The expansion project will add a capacity of 40 million passengers annually, bringing Cairo International Airport’s total capacity to 70 million passengers per year.

This strategic investment aligns with Egypt Vision 2030, reinforcing the nation’s position as a premier regional transit hub connecting Africa, Asia, and Europe while supporting tourism, trade, and overall economic growth.

World.title: US dollar drops against Egyptian Pound following surge in CBE foreign reserves
World.content:
The Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) announced that its net international foreign exchange reserves rose to $56.30 billion at the end of July.

This increase reflects the ongoing improvement in the country’s foreign liquidity position and strengthens the Egyptian economy’s ability to fulfill its international obligations.

Official data released by the CBE revealed a monthly increase of approximately $600 million compared to June’s level of $55.70 billion.

This continuous upward trajectory serves as a crucial buffer to protect the local economy from external shocks. It ensures the provision of foreign currency needed to finance imports and strategic goods while facilitating the timely repayment of external obligations and debts.

Furthermore, this improvement grants the Central Bank greater flexibility in managing monetary policy and maintaining foreign exchange market stability.

This boosts the confidence of international investors and financial institutions in the prospects of the Egyptian economy and its ability to navigate changing challenges.

Following the announcement, the US dollar exchange rate experienced a noticeable drop against the Egyptian pound, continuing the local currency’s upward trend.

Dollar rates in most operating local banks fell by up to 75 piasters, dropping back below the LE 50 mark in some institutions.

Data issued by banks showed the greenback trading in ranges between LE 49.50 and LE 50.25 for buying, and between LE 49.60 and LE 50.35 for selling.

World.title: Egypt bans Australian alternative health figure Barbara O’Neill over false claims
World.content:
Egypt’s Supreme Council for Media Regulation (SCMR) has decided to ban Australian alternative healthcare promoter Barbara O’Neill from appearing across media outlets due to her false health claims, Veto reported.

The Council ruled to prohibit broadcasting, rebroadcasting, or distributing any video content featuring her, and banned the promotion of any health, training, or event services she offers within Egypt.

The decision follows official communications received by the SCMR from the Ministry of Health and Population and the Egyptian Medical Syndicate.

These communications revealed that O’Neill lacks legal status and holds no license to practice medicine, as she is not registered with the Ministry’s medical registry or the Egyptian Medical Syndicate, nor does she possess any recognized qualification in medicine or therapeutic nutrition.

Consequently, providing any diagnostic or therapeutic content subjects her to the prohibitions established under Law #415 of 1954 regarding the practice of human medicine.

Furthermore, a permanent regulatory ban was issued against her abroad by the New South Wales Health Care Complaints Commission in Australia on September 24, 2019, prohibiting her from providing any health or awareness services or delivering lectures, whether paid or voluntary.

The authorities also highlighted her promotion of dangerous claims which would negatively impact public health.

These include promoting scientifically unproven treatments for tumors, advocating the replacement of breastfeeding for infants with animal milk, downplaying the efficacy of antibiotics, and opposing vaccinations.

Such claims undermine long-standing national health programs and encourage patients to delay or abandon specialized medical treatment, thereby endangering their lives.

Additionally, she intentionally misleads audiences by adopting academic and medical titles unsupported by any genuine qualifications.

World.title: FRA depots bring relief To Lavushimanda maize farmers
World.content:
Farmers in Mupamadzi ward of Lavushimanda District in Muchinga Province have thanked Government for bringing the Food Reserve Agency (FRA) maize depots closer to them.

‎This follows the opening of four satellite deports in the area, which started operating last maize marketing season.

‎One of the Farmers, Poster Kunda stated that the opening of the Kalonje Mpanga satellite depot by the Government in the area has assisted in addressing the high cost of transportation of Maize, thereby reducing post-harvest losses.

‎Mr Kunda has however asked government to ensure that a shelter is put on the satellite depot in order to secure the maize and protect it from the rains and sun.

‎“I commend the government for this depot because most of us use to suffer loses in transporting our maize to another deport, which is far from here”, he said.

‎Another Farmer, Pressley Mupeta echoed similar sentiments stating that he used to cover a long distance of over five kilometres to transport his maize to Mupamadzi maize deport at a high cost.

‎He said the opening of Kalonje Mpanga Maize depot now allows farmers to easily transport their maize using available means of transport such as bicycles or ox-cart because the distance has been reduced as he also thanked government for the development.

‎“I can now manage to use available transport to bring my maize here and for this reason, I thank government for bringing our maize market closer”, he said.

‎And Lavushimanda District Commissioner, Terries Kunda who recently visited the area and talked to the farmers said government will address the concerns of farmers such as network challenges and lack of equipment’s such as sieves.

‎Mr Kunda also assured farmers that no Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA) tax will be deducted from their monies received after selling Maize to FRA, adding that the issue of mobile network challenges raised by farmers will also be addressed.

‎“Our government is attending to all your concerns and be rest assured that no ZRA tax will be deducted from your money apart from the little normal transaction amounts being deducted by your mobile service providers”, he said.

‎Among the concerns raised by farmers in Kalonje Mpanga include poor mobile network, inadequate sieves and high illiterate levels by some farmers who are unable to read and write when they receive any communication from FRA with regard to the selling of Maize.

‎According to FRA Assistant Marketing Officer for Lavushimanda, Fredrick Simwaba, last year, the government opened four additional maize satellite deports in the area, bringing the total number of depots to 18 while the area has three main maize holding deports.

World.title: President Hichilema Pledges to formalise Mufumbwe’s Kikonge Mine
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has promised to finalise the formalisation of the Kikonge mine in Mufumbwe District in Northwestern Province if re-elected in the August 13 general elections.

President Hichilema says he will ensure that the mine employs the local people so that they also get empowered.

He said he will ensure that the locals are given the necessary equipment so that they mine safely.

“Am not going to allow foreigners to be employed at Kikonge, I want the local people from Mufumbwe to be employed,” said President Hichilema.

President Hichilema said he will ensure to give many mining licences to the locals that will be conducting mining activities at Kikonge mine.

The Head of State has called on residents of Mufumbwe district to vote for the UPND party for continued development in the area.

President Hichilema explained that voting for the UPND party will enable the residents to continue enjoying the incentives such as Cash for work, increased Constituency Development Fund (CDF) and the Social Cash Transfer.

Speaking during a community engagement at Jairos Fumpa Secondary School grounds this afternoon, President Hichilema stated that voting for UPND will see the expansion of the Mufumbwe Prisons which is small.

President Hichilema disclosed that his priority is to work on the township roads such as Kalengwa- Kabipupu and M8 roads.

“We are going to work on the Kalengwa-Kabipupu and the M8 roads that are in a deplorable state,” stated President Hichilema.

The Head of State has also pledged to expand the Mufumbwe district hospital that will have many departments in order to avoid referrals to bigger hospitals.

“We will expand the Mifumbwe district hospital into a bigger one. We will ensure the expanded one will have many units so that we avoid reffering patients to other hospitals,” he said.

Meanwhile, President Hichilema has re -emphasised that Kalengwa mining jobs should be given to the locals stressing that not people from other regions.

” We opened the Kalengwa mine after 40 years of being closed, so we want residents of Mufumbwe to be employed so that they are also empowered not employing people from other parts of the country,” President Hichilema noted.

He said he wants to legalise mining at Kikonge mine so that the resident can mine safely.

President Hichilema said he will give more licences to the residents to be mining from Kikonge .

“We will ensure to give the residents the necessary equipment to the residents to mine at Kikonge, we will also provide a market for them to sell their gold,” said President Hichilema.

“I don’t want Kikonge people to be fighting like in Eastern Congo,” President Hichilema stated.

He also instructed that the volunteer nurses that attended the engagement should be employed next month.

The Head of State has also promised to give Stephen Masumba employment for being loyal to him and the party.

“Masumba, am happy that you have been so loyal to the party. You wanted to contest but the party did not adopt you but you behaved yourself. Therefore, I promise to give you a job after August 13,” said President Hichilema.

President Hichilema further stated that if re -elected, his government will ensure that Mufumbwe has more satelite depots.

“We are going to increase the fertiliser for farmers stressing that they will no longer be sharing a bucket,” said President Hichilema.

He also disclosed that if re- elected, he will ensure early distribution of FISP across the country.

And the Chairperson for the Kikonge Mining Consortium has expressed gratitude with the President’s pronouncements on Kikonge mine stating that they have been looking forward to the formalisation.

World.title: Distribution of ballot papers to conclude tomorrow – ECZ
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) says the distribution of ballot papers for the August 13 General Elections which commenced on August 2nd, will conclude on tomorrow, August 8th, 2026.

Speaking during a stakeholders’ engagement in Lusaka, ECZ Acting Director of Electoral Operations, Winner Mwanamonga, also disclosed that training of over 81, 000 poll staff is currently underway with deployment scheduled for August 10th to 12th.

Mr Mwanamonga also announced that 8.7 million voters were updated in the register for the August 13th General Elections with 53 percent being females and 46 percent, males.

Following the delimitation exercise, Mr Mwanamonga noted that the country now has 13, 529 polling stations from 1,858 wards of the 226 Constituencies.

He added that a total of 14 Presidential candidates, 973 Parliamentary and 439 Mayoral candidates as well as 5,099 aspiring councilors are currently contesting in this year’s general elections.

Mr Mwanamonga further indicated that the first ever Presidential Campaign timetable introduced ahead of this year’s general elections has enhanced the Commission’s management of the 2026 campaigns.

He also expressed satisfaction with progress of publicity and conflict management, so far.

“Chair, I’m happy to report that if you drive around, there are more voter education posters than any other posters,” he said.

Earlier, ECZ Chairperson, Mwangala Zaloumis who officially opened the meeting, reminded stakeholders, especially political parties of their responsibility to guard against misinformation in order to contribute to an informed electorate and promote trust in the electoral process.

Mrs Zaloumis expressed disappointment with the absence of some political parties at the meeting, urging them to take such engagements seriously.

She further encouraged stakeholders to rely on verified information and ensure that only accurate details are shared with members, supporters, and the wider public.

“By doing so, we can collectively minimise the spread of misinformation and disinformation and strengthen public confidence in the electoral process,” she added.

Meanwhile, ECZ Chief Electoral Officer, Brown Kasaro, disclosed that Voter Verification Devices will not be used during this year’s election as the Commission does not have resources to procure some.

“The plan was a 100 percent roll-out of the VVDs. So it’s either 100 percent or we will not deploy at all,” he said.

World.title: UG President calls for peace ahead of August 13 polls
World.content:
The Zambia Union of Government and Allied Workers (UG) has called on political parties and their supporters across the country to maintain peace and avoid violence ahead of the August 13 General Elections.

UG President, Muyaywa Kabisa, has further urged political leaders to exercise control over their members and ensure that the electoral process remains peaceful.

Dr Kabisa notes that peace is a defining characteristic of Zambians and should not be compromised by political differences.

The UG President, in an interview in Lusaka today, said he is disturbed by reports of political violence in some parts of the country which are allegedly painting a negative picture of the electoral process and undermining public confidence in elections.

He said violence will not help any candidate win an election, but instead risks eroding the confidence that citizens have invested in that political party.

Dr Kabisa reminded political leaders and their supporters that violence has the potential of fueling ‘war’ like was experienced in other countries.

He has also urged citizens to exercise their constitutional right and vote in next week’s general polls.

World.title: Zambia, DRC Strengthen Trade Ties Through Bilateral Talks
World.content:
Zambia and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have held bilateral talks in Ndola aimed at strengthening cross-border trade and addressing challenges affecting the movement of transit goods between the two neighbouring countries.

Government says it will introduce stringent measures at all border entry and exit points to curb the illegal offloading of transit cargo in Zambia before it reaches its final destination in the DRC, a practice that has resulted in revenue losses for the DRC and heightened smuggling concerns.

Speaking during the bilateral meeting held at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium, Ministry of Commerce, Trade and Industry Permanent Secretary Lilian Bwalya said Zambia and the DRC must work together to combat illegal trade practices, strengthen border security and ensure that all transit cargo reaches its intended destination.

Ms Bwalya said the illegal diversion of transit goods negatively affects customs revenue in both countries, as goods meant to pass through Zambia are offloaded and sold locally without payment of the required duties.

“We are determined to fight all forms of crime, especially smuggling, because it also affects our revenue. Goods that are supposed to transit through Zambia are dumped on the market without paying taxes,” she said.

Ms Bwalya stressed that all goods imported into Zambia must pay the applicable taxes, while goods in transit should be allowed to proceed to their final destination without interference.

She further urged the two governments to implement an electronic data exchange system to enable authorities to monitor cargo before it reaches the border.

“We appeal to our two governments to ensure that data exchange is implemented. With this system, it becomes easier to share information before the cargo even arrives at the border,” she said.

Ms Bwalya also proposed the establishment of a One-Stop Border Post Where Zambian and DRC officials would jointly clear cargo destined for the DRC, saying this would improve monitoring and reduce the diversion of transit goods.

Meanwhile, Democratic Republic of Congo’s Haut-Katanga Province Acting Governor Martin Kazembe said the DRC government has already introduced measures to curb the illegal practice of cargo fractioning, which he said is harming the country’s economy and creating unfair competition.

Mr Kazembe said the measures were being implemented in collaboration with the central government.

“We have started arresting those involved in cargo fractioning, but we cannot do it alone. That is why the central government mandated me to engage with Zambia because we are neighbours today and forever,” he said.

He called on Zambia to support the measures in order to strengthen economic, security and health cooperation between the two countries.

Mr Kazembe further said measures introduced to curb copper cathode theft in the DRC have produced positive results but require continued collaboration and adequate resources.

He also assured Zambia of enhanced security along the shared border ahead of next week’s elections and proposed the establishment of a joint commission for Sakania.

“I would like to thank you for the resolutions that have been made here. I assure you of our commitment to maintaining security during your electoral period,” he said.

Mr Kazembe also called on authorities managing other border posts between Zambia and the DRC to work closely with security agencies to ensure a peaceful electoral period.

World.title: Chadiza authorities renew commitment to breastfeeding support systems
World.content:
Authorities in Chadiza District have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening support systems for breastfeeding mothers, as the world commemorates World Breastfeeding Week.

Speaking during the commemoration held under the theme “Breastfeeding for a Sustainable Start in Life: Strengthen What Works”, Acting District Commissioner (DC) Masauso Mwale said although Zambia continues to perform well in breastfeeding compared to many countries, recent data shows that exclusive breastfeeding rates have declined.

“Some mothers stop exclusive breastfeeding too early because of misinformation, pressure to introduce other foods, work commitments or inadequate family and community support,” he said.

The Acting DC noted that challenges such as myths, marketing of breast milk substitutes, and lack of support at workplaces are affecting breastfeeding practices.

He however said the district has made progress through health facilities, outreach services, Safe Motherhood Action Groups and community nutrition support groups.

And District Nutritionist Ireen Ndoti said breastfeeding benefits mothers by reducing the risk of excessive bleeding after childbirth and lowering the risk of breast and ovarian cancers, type 2 diabetes and other chronic diseases.

“With this said, I call on employers to create breastfeeding-friendly workplaces to help mothers continue breastfeeding after returning to work,” he said.

World.title: Mighty defender Kakungu jailed for assault
World.content:
Mufulira Wanderers defender Bwembya Kakungu has been jailed for six months after being convicted of assault by the Mufulira Court.

The Super Division club confirmed the development in a statement, noting that the former Mighty captain remains detained in prison.

“Mufulira Wanderers Football Club has taken note of the conviction and subsequent six-month prison sentence handed down to our player, Bwembya Kakungu, for assault,” the club board said.

“The Club respects the decision of the Court and wishes to state that violence and assault have no place in Mufulira Wanderers Football Club, football or society.”

Sources close to the player say disciplinary issues negatively affected Kakungu’s performance in the 2025/26 campaign.

After putting in incredible performances in previous seasons, Kakungu, hampered by injuries, did not see match action last term.

Kakungu also has national team experience. In June 2023, he was part of the Chipolopolo squad that faced Kuwait in a friendly match.

The club said it upholds values of discipline, respect and responsible conduct, both on and off the field.

“The Club is reviewing the matter in accordance with its internal policies, the player’s contractual obligations and applicable football regulations,”_ the statement added.

“Any further decision regarding the player’s status will be communicated through the appropriate channels.”

Kakungu has a contract with Mighty stretching to June 2027.

World.title: Kawana reminds media of their responsibilities
World.content:
Media houses in Zambia have been advised to exercise professionalism and responsibility as they cover the forthcoming general elections in the country

Ministry of Information and Media Permanent Secretary, Thabo Kawana urged journalists and editors to avoid sensational reporting but instead adhere to the ethical principles of journalism by verifying facts, presenting balanced stories, and seeking all sides of an issue before publication or broadcast.

Mr Kawana said at a press briefing in Lusaka that there is a need for journalists to help safeguard peace and national unity during and after elections.

He further cautioned media organisations against publishing misinformation or disinformation, saying responsible journalism is essential during the electoral period.

He said the country has entered a critical period hence the media should ensure that their reporting does not fuel tension or confusion.

Mr Kawana also reminded media houses that the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) is the only official body mandated to announce election results.

He further advised media organisations to refrain from broadcasting or publishing unofficial election tallies and instead rely solely on results officially released by the ECZ.

Mr Kawana warned that publishing unofficial results, including exit polls or figures based on Parallel Vote Tabulation (PVT), could create unnecessary confusion among the public.

Meanwhile, Mr Kawana has expressed concern over the conduct of some named broadcasting stations, stating that their recent actions leave much to be desired.

The Ministry of Information and Media Permanent Secretary has since called on the management of the named media houses to closely monitor the work of their reporters and editors to ensure compliance with professional and ethical standards throughout the election period.
