World.title: Apple officially enters Iraq under new digital services framework
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Apple has legally joined Iraq’s regulated digital market, having met the country’s standards for digital platforms and services, according to the Communications and Media Commission (CMC).

According to the regulator, Apple has been categorized as a trusted digital service provider in Iraq, which includes the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Podcasts, Apple Arcade, and Apple Ads.

The certification means Apple’s digital services may now function under an official Iraqi regulatory framework, having passed the CMC’s technical and legal standards.

Iraqi officials said the decision is anticipated to boost the country’s digital economy and enhance the investment climate for multinational technology firms.

The development also corresponds with a significant step toward Apple’s physical presence in the Iraqi market. Asiacell has reached a direct arrangement with Apple to include iPhones in its retail network across Iraq.

As part of the cooperation, Asiacell will provide real Apple products with valid warranties throughout its network, while retail personnel will undergo Apple-approved training.

The regulatory permission and Asiacell deal represent a substantial change in Apple’s position in Iraq, pushing both digital services and official device distribution further into a market of over 46 million people.

The move is another indication of Iraq’s quickly emerging technology and consumer market, as Baghdad attempts to lure global corporations, legalize digital services, and promote increased investment in the country’s information technology industry.

World.title: Al-Ghodwa deploys Linde warehouse equipment in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Linde Material Handling of Germany has completed a new warehouse technology project in Baghdad with its official Iraqi partner, Al-Ghodwa Group, as modern logistics systems gain traction in Iraq.

The project was completed in early August, and it comprised the installation and commissioning of two Linde Very Narrow Aisle (VNA) trucks built for high-density warehouse operations.

As part of the turnkey project, Al-Ghodwa installed the guiding system, calibrated and tested the equipment, and taught the local operators.

The technology enables firms to store more items in their current warehouse space by running equipment securely in tighter lanes, which increases productivity and reduces space needs.

The project combines Linde’s German warehouse technology with local installation, maintenance, and after-sales services in Iraq.

Linde Material Handling is a subsidiary of Germany’s KION Group, one of the world’s biggest producers of industrial vehicles and a leading supplier of warehouse automation systems.

The Baghdad installation comes as Iraq’s logistics and distribution industry grows, amid investment in manufacturing, retail, transportation, and private-sector growth.

World.title: Saudi renews invitation to Iraq PM as Baghdad, Riyadh seek to repair ties
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Saudi Arabia has extended an invitation to Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi to visit Riyadh as the two countries try to regain momentum in ties after a dangerous escalation involving Iran-backed militias operating from Iraqi soil.

Al-Zaidi met with Saudi intelligence head Khalid bin Ali Al-Humaidan in Baghdad on Friday, with the Saudi official conveying a message from the kingdom’s leadership extending the offer and discussing greater security cooperation, according to the Iraqi government.

The meeting is notable since Al-Zaidi canceled a scheduled visit to Saudi Arabia last month in response to US-Saudi airstrikes on Iran-aligned armed groups in Iraq.

These operations followed a series of drone assaults on Saudi Arabia.

Riyadh claimed that Iran-backed militias fired drones from Iraqi territory, attempting to damage oil installations in the Eastern Province and targets near Riyadh, and publicly urged Baghdad to prevent its land from being used as a launchpad for assaults against the country.

Saudi Arabia then launched operations with US troops against Iran-backed militia strongholds in Iraq, increasing pressure on Baghdad to bring armed organizations operating outside of effective official control under its authority.

During Friday’s meeting, Al-Zaidi underlined Iraq’s refusal to allow its land to be used for attacks on Saudi Arabia or any other country, emphasizing Baghdad’s commitment to sovereignty, good neighbor relations, and regional security.

According to the Iraqi statement, the two sides agreed to maintain information sharing and security cooperation, with Baghdad aiming to avoid future assaults that may prompt another military reaction on Iraqi soil.

The outreach coincides with Saudi Arabia’s efforts to deepen regional security relationships.

On Friday, Riyadh, Ankara, and Islamabad signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, which states that any military assault on one of the three nations is considered an attack on all.

Saudi authorities are also apprehensive about additional strikes by Iran-aligned forces.

For Al-Zaidi, the repeated Saudi invitation provides a chance to mend ties with one of Iraq’s most significant Arab neighbors while also displaying Baghdad’s determination to prevent Iran-backed forces from dictating its regional connections.

The implications extend beyond security. Iraq has been pursuing more Saudi and Gulf investment as part of a larger push to diversify its economy, attract foreign money, and enhance trade and infrastructural ties with its Arab neighbors.

As a result, Friday’s meeting constitutes a crucial step in moving Baghdad-Riyadh relations past last month’s dispute. However, continued progress is likely to be strongly dependent on Iraq’s capacity to show that attacks on its neighbors would not be launched from its territory in the future.

World.title: Spain imposes border checks on Italy as migrant showdown grows
World.content:
Madrid – Spain announced on Friday it would introduce temporary border checks on travellers from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures after a mass migrant rush into Ceuta.

The checks, which come “amid the persistent irregular migration pressure” facing Italy, will start at midnight on Saturday and last until September 7, Spain’s interior ministry said in a statement.

Hours earlier, Spain threatened Italy with countermeasures if it did not swiftly lift its own border checks, drawing a rebuff from Rome.

The rare spat between the European Union and NATO allies came after tens of thousands of people crossed from Morocco to Spain’s North African territory on July 30-31 in an unprecedented, deadly rush.

The scenes infuriated EU members that back a hard line on irregular immigration, including Italy which imposed a one-month suspension of its visa free-travel Schengen deal with Spain.

The Spanish government slammed the measure Friday as “unfair, contrary to the EU’s interests and discriminatory for the Spanish population”.

Foreign Minister Jose Manuel Albares described it as “a torpedo fired at the hull of European unity.”

“We urge the government of Italy to rectify, put an end to the checks and treat Spaniards like other European citizens,” the government said.

He threatened “proportional measures” in response by Sunday if Italy failed to comply.

– ‘Creating rifts’ –

Within hours, the government of Italy’s far-right Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said it “had no intention of revising the decision” before August 15, when it said Spanish authorities “expected a new wave of migration” to hit Ceuta.

“Italy does not accept ultimatums or impositions from abroad regarding national security and border control,” Meloni’s office said in a statement.

“Only when there is certainty that there are no security or terrorism risks to Italy, that no new wave is occurring, and that no irregular migrants are heading toward European territory, will the decision be reconsidered,” it read.

Spain’s interior ministry announced the reciprocal measures within hours.

Spanish police have been monitoring online rumours and social media about possible fresh arrivals in Ceuta in mid-August, according to local media. But authorities have not expressly said they expect a repeat of last week’s rush.

Border authorities would in the meantime “do their utmost to ensure maximum ease of movement for Spanish and European citizens” who are not affected by border checks, the Italian statement added.

Italy, which does not share a land border with Spain, introduced border controls at maritime and air entry points for third-country nationals arriving from the Iberian country.

The move announced on July 31 was an “extraordinary measure” intended to “safeguard national security and prevent possible repercussions for our nation”, Meloni said at the time.

She was among EU leaders who called for Spain to be suspended from the visa-free Schengen travel zone after the Ceuta incident, despite such a move being legally impossible.

Italy’s coalition government has sought to stop the tens of thousands of people who land in small boats on the country’s shores each year.

The Spanish government warned against “creating rifts and sterile conflicts driven by internal electoral motives” and said “we trust that pro-European sentiment, common sense and good faith prevail”.

Of the 72,000 people who entered Ceuta, 70,000 have returned to Morocco, according to official Spanish figures.

Spanish authorities said 80 people died in the crossings.

Moroccan rights groups however estimate the figure to be higher. The Moroccan Association for Human Rights (AMDH) and the European Coordination for Human Rights in Morocco on Friday said at least 141 deaths were recorded and that the toll was likely to rise.

Morocco’s interior ministry has said 11 people died on its side of the border, all but one by drowning.

Those who remain in Ceuta — including hundreds of unaccompanied children — face dire living conditions with little access to food, water, and shelter.

World.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan sign defence pact amid regional war
World.content:
Riyadh – Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement on Friday amid violence in the region from Houthi attacks and the US-Iran war.

Riyadh is looking to strengthen its security ties against the backdrop of war between the United States and Iran, which has drawn in surrounding nations and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.

The war has emboldened Iran and its Houthi allies in Yemen, both of which have attacked Saudi Arabia, while analysts say Washington is now seen as an increasingly unreliable partner.

In a joint statement published by the official Saudi press agency and Pakistan’s foreign ministry, the three countries announced the signing of the “Mecca Joint Defence Agreement”.

They declared a “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security and stability in the region and beyond”.

Pakistan’s foreign ministry said the pact meant an attack on any member would be regarded as an attack on all, adding it was “intended to strengthen collective deterrence”.

Ankara nonetheless said later that the agreement was “not aimed at any particular country”, according to a post on X by the presidency’s communications director.

It added that “the agreement is not in contradiction with the commitments of Turkey’s existing international alliances, including those at the heart of NATO,” according to a post on X by the government’s anti-disinformation service.

Riyadh said “the agreement does not represent an effort to establish a military axis or a sectarian bloc”.

“Nor is it linked to any nuclear ambitions or arms race, rather it is focused on building sustainable capabilities,” Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said on X.

The “does not constitute a threat to the security of any country in the region”, he added.

– ‘Layers of security’ –

Since the onset of the regional war, Saudi Arabia has grown closer to Turkey, Egypt and Pakistan, which have been pushing for mediation and a resolution to the conflict.

Umar Karim, an expert on Saudi foreign policy at the University of Birmingham, England, said the alignment “is clearly oriented towards Iran and meant to address Iran’s new strategic approach which is geared towards dominance of the broader Gulf region”.

The fact that Turkey and Pakistan border Iran means they could “exercise a different kind of leverage” on Tehran, he added.

A source close to the Saudi military and government told AFP before the signing that although the agreement had been under discussion for a long time, “the latest developments in the region expedite it”.

Andreas Krieg of King’s College London said the deal showed a clear desire to diversify alliances beyond the United States.

“Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are not trying to replace the United States,” he said.

“They are building the capacity to protect their interests when Washington cannot or will not do so.”

Riyadh, in particular, he added, “wants several layers of security rather than one American umbrella”, after the shock of the Iran war.

The deal will support Saudi Arabia’s ambitions to become an organiser of regional security and diversify its defence umbrella, said Krieg. Turkey and Pakistan gain political clout and access to potential Saudi investments, he added.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Mecca on Friday, the Turkish presidency said on X, sharing an image of the meeting.

Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and army chief Asim Munir also travelled to the Gulf kingdom for the signing.

– Renewed Houthi attacks –

Saudi Arabia and Pakistan had already announced a mutual defence pact in 2025, a move that drew attention because Pakistan is the Muslim world’s only nuclear-armed state.

The deal also comes as a truce between Riyadh and the Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen has broken down. The Houthis have launched attacks on Saudi soil and declared a maritime blockade against Saudi Arabia, which they have attempted to enforce by attacking Saudi tankers.

The Houthis, backed by Iran, have added pressure to Gulf energy exporters — already under strain from Tehran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz — by threatening Red Sea shipping.

Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government against the Houthis since 2015.

A truce was agreed four years ago which largely held until hostilities broke out again in recent weeks.

On Thursday, the Houthis killed at least 58 Yemeni government troops in missile and drone attacks, a military source said, in one of the conflict’s deadliest days in years.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate continues to rise in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,523.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,520.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,530 Iraqi dinars and 1,520 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,525.5 and 1,525 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq to increase production from Kirkuk oil fields
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair announced on Thursday plans to increase oil production from the Kirkuk oilfields.

The decision intends to capitalize on a recent agreement with Turkey for exporting oil to the port of Ceyhan.

This move also aims to circumvent the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and increase Iraq’s oil exports via ports on the Mediterranean.

The instruction utilizes the recently expanded Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline deal, with the goal of increasing exports from 180,000 barrels per day to approximately 750,000 barrels per day.

Khudair stated that increasing production lays the groundwork for boosting export volumes through Turkey to 1.5 million barrels per day.

Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO) has officially partnered with British Petroleum (BP) to bolster cooperation in oil and natural gas projects in Kirkuk oilfields.

In 2025, BP reached a deal with Iraq’s North Oil Company (NOC) to develop oil fields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk, with investments projected to reach $25 billion.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s attempts to optimize energy sector investments, increase oil output, and minimize gas flaring.

The enhanced output directly addresses the Iraqi government’s growing deficit as a result of continued maritime restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

By producing more petroleum from Kirkuk, Baghdad reduces internal shipping expenses from southern fields while increasing supplies to global markets via outlets on the Mediterranean.

World.title: Iraqi Prime Minister orders higher military readiness as security tensions rise
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces Ali Al-Zaidi has directed all security and military formations to raise their operational readiness and combat preparedness, according to the Security Media Cell.

The directive aims to maintain a high state of preparedness across Iraq’s security forces through intensified training exercises and operational movements designed to strengthen national security and protect public interests.

In a statement, the Security Media Cell said the Commander-in-Chief instructed security and military forces to increase their level of readiness while conducting training exercises and field movements.

The measures are intended to ensure that all security formations remain fully prepared to carry out their assigned duties and respond to potential security developments.

According to the statement, the directive is part of ongoing efforts to maintain continuous operational readiness across Iraq’s armed forces.

The Security Media Cell said the enhanced readiness program is designed to reinforce Iraq’s security framework and improve the capabilities of military and security units.

Officials stated that maintaining high readiness contributes to:

Strengthening national security.

Preserving public stability.

Protecting Iraqi citizens.

Safeguarding public institutions and national interests.

The government has increasingly emphasized preparedness amid evolving regional security challenges.

The announcement comes during a period of elevated security concerns in Iraq following recent regional developments and heightened tensions involving armed groups.

The official statement, however, does not specify any particular threat or military operation linked to the readiness order.

Some media reports and political analysts have suggested the move may be connected to broader security developments or precautionary planning ahead of upcoming government deadlines. These assessments are analytical interpretations and were not included in the official Security Media Cell statement.

The latest directive reflects Baghdad’s continued focus on ensuring the operational effectiveness of Iraq’s security institutions.

By ordering additional training activities and maintaining high alert levels, the government aims to preserve stability while ensuring security forces remain prepared to respond to any developments affecting the country’s security environment.

World.title: Opposition wants Amit Shah in House; government says 'not your call'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Amid continuing opposition protests lampooning home minister

for his "absence" from the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, parliamentary affairs minister

Friday said the opposition cannot decide which minister will come to the House and speak.

With the Lok Sabha paralysed and a virtual washout of Parliament's monsoon session looming, Rijiju said Shah comes to Parliament building every day and stays till late at night. "Shah is a man whose name sends shivers down the spine of extremists and terrorists," he said, amid the thumping of desks by members of the treasury benches. "The day the discussion begins here, and when Amit Shah responds, you (opposition) won't be able to sit through it," he said.

Protests by opposition MPs forced the chairs of both Houses to adjourn the proceedings till Monday. The opposition has put Shah at the centre of its protests against alleged police excesses against protesters organised under the banner of Cockroach Janta Party who defied prohibitory orders to march towards Parliament. The Lok Sabha could not function as opposition MPs held placards and raised slogans demanding that Shah come to the House and respond to the police action on student protesters.

World.title: Tribunal reforms bill gets nod, paves way for national body
World.content:
NEW DELHIL: The Cabinet on Thursday approved the Tribunals Reforms Bill that will have the provision for setting up a National Tribunal Commission (NTC), which has been visualised as an independent body to supervise appointments and functioning of around 16 tribunals and look after their administrative and infrastructural needs.

Minister of state for parliamentary affairs L Murugan informed the Rajya Sabha on Friday that the bill will be introduced in the Lok Sabha. TOI has learnt that NTC will be headed by a retired SC or high court judge for five years or till he or she turns 70 years.

People aware of the proposal said the government has proposed the body at the instance of the

.

The apex court had ordered the constitution of NTC first in May 2018. It reiterated its directive in 2020.

In November last year, SC stressed that the government has a constitutional obligation to establish NTC and gave it four months to constitute the commission, and lamented that its directions had not been heeded.

In June, the Supreme Court expressed serious concern over the functioning of tribunals across the country, with CJI Surya Kant observing that these bodies have become "a liability for the judiciary" and "a headache" for the government.

World.title: Supeme Court to Mahua: Freedom fighters faced bullets, you fear eggs
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Friday dismissed TMC MP

's plea seeking permission to appear virtually before police in a case against her for uploading a provocative post on Facebook.

As the MP took the ground that she will be attacked by a mob if she physically went there and eggs may be thrown at her, a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said, "You are an MP? Having taken the plunge into politics, you fear eggs? When our freedom fighters have taken bullets on their chest? These are applications that should not come before this court at all.

"

Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for the MP, contended before the bench that she should be permitted to appear before the investigation officer through video conferencing.

"Why virtually? Because you are an MP?" the court asked.

World.title: Supreme Court seeks Bihar minister's record of appointment & nomination as MLC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday sought records from the Bihar government relating to the appointment of Deepak Prakash, who was not a member of the assembly, as a minister in Nov last year, his re-induction into the cabinet in May and his recent hurried nomination as an MLC allegedly to skirt around the six-month deadline within which such a minister must get elected to the House.

A PIL has challenged his continuance as minister after the expiry of the six-month deadline within which a person, who is not a member of the assembly or legislative council, must get elected as a member of either house.

Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, for the Bihar government, told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi, and V Mohana that the minister has since been nominated as an MLC by the governor; hence, his continuance was not unconstitutional.

However, the petitioner, relying on the SC's 2001 judgment in the SR Chaudhari case, which had categorically stated that the six-month deadline was non-negotiable, said the six-month deadline expired on May 20. With Nitish Kumar stepping down as CM on April 15, the council of ministers was dissolved. The new council of ministers was constituted under Samrat Choudhary on May 7, which included Prakash. The bench asked the Bihar government to place on record all documents relating to the appointment of Prakash in the first instance, his re-induction and subsequent nomination as MLC.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





In its 2001 judgment by a three-judge bench, SC had ruled, "Permitting a non-legislator minister to be re-appointed, without getting elected within the period prescribed by Article 164(4) (six months), would amount to ignoring the electorate in having its say as to who should represent it - a position which is wholly unacceptable.

"The seductive temptations to cling to office regardless of constitutional restraint must be totally eschewed. Will of the people cannot be permitted to be subordinated to political expediency of the prime minister or the chief minister as the case may be, to have in his cabinet a non-legislator as a minister for an indefinite period by repeated re-appointments without the individual seeking popular mandate of the electorate.

"

The SC added, "Chief ministers or governors must... not sacrifice either political responsibility or parliamentary conventions at the altar of political expediency."

World.title: No conflict of interest in RDI Fund, says government
World.content:
Since its establishment under an Act of Parliament in 1996, TDB has relied upon independent expert committees rather than individual officials for evaluating technology proposals

NEW DELHI: The government on Friday said the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund is being implemented through a robust institutional framework with "stringent conflict-of-interest safeguards" in place, highlighting that it is designed "not to exclude domain expertise but to regulate it through clearly defined conflict-of-interest provisions".Rebutting a media report that 15 of the 22 entities that got public funds to boost India's deep-tech ambitions have investment links to seven members of the selection committee, raising questions of conflict of interest and propriety, Technology Development Board (TDB) secretary Rajesh Kumar Pathak said the mere existence of a professional or investment association with an innovation ecosystem entity does not constitute a violation of conflict-of-interest norms."What the framework requires is full disclosure of such interests and complete recusal from the evaluation and decision-making process relating to the proposal concerned... All members had, accordingly, recused themselves, and each decision was taken not by simple majority but by super-majority (two-thirds) of eligible members," said Pathak."Members who declare a conflict of interest neither participate in discussions nor vote on the concerned proposal."Pathak also underlined that TDB has "consistently followed similar conflict-of-interest safeguards for nearly three decades" while supporting indigenous technology development.Since its establishment under an Act of Parliament in 1996, TDB has relied upon independent expert committees rather than individual officials for evaluating technology proposals.The same institutional principles continue to govern project selection under the RDI Fund, reinforcing continuity, credibility and public confidence in the decision-making process, he added.Prof Umesh V Waghmare, secretary in the department of science and technology and TDB chairperson, said the government has followed the conflict-of-interest guidelines and framework diligently and strongly believes that there have been no violations. TDB is one of the agencies selected to grant money under the Centre's Rs 1 lakh crore RDI Fund. It has, so far, approved assistance for 22 projects involving Rs 2,192 crore of financing.

NEW DELHI: The information and broadcasting (I&B) ministry has told a parliamentary committee that it is mulling a comprehensive statutory framework to regulate the airing of programmes on OTT platforms, "which are offensive to moral standards of society", without infringing upon the rights and freedom of individuals.The department-related standing committee on the ministry of home affairs, in its recommendations in the 259th report tabled in Parliament on Friday, said the proposed comprehensive statutory framework for regulating OTT content must incorporate robust technology-enabled age verification mechanisms, effective parental controls and suitable penalties for non-compliance.While observing that the existing framework continued to rely largely on self-regulation by OTT platforms, the committee - in its recommendations on the action taken on its 254th report - reiterated that the government examine the feasibility of establishing an independent post-release review panel - comprising experts from fields like child development, education, law, social sciences and civil society - to review flagged OTT content and lay down appropriate corrective measures.The panel had, in its 254th report, said, "OTT platforms have emerged as a primary source of entertainment in India, with a reach that surpasses traditional cinema, including a substantial audience of minors." The committee pointed out that unlike films, which require mandatory pre-certification under the Cinematograph Act, OTT content operates under a self-classification system with post-release grievance redressal as per the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021.The panel said that although the aforesaid rules require age ratings, parental controls and a grievance mechanism, the lack of pre-release checks and weak age verification still leaves minors exposed to harmful content. Accordingly, it recommended that the government consider establishing a recognised panel of experts who will monitor new OTT releases.It suggested that the post-release review panel watch the flagged or trending content based on user complaints submitted through a standardised grievance mechanism.The panel, it said, shall devise suitable norms and guidelines "keeping in view the cultural ethos and sensitivity of the country". It recommended that the panel also work out suitable penalties for infringement of these norms/guidelines.

World.title: Share data on river waters, India tells China
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In another round of diplomatic engagement on the border issue, India and China had âfrank discussionsâ and reviewed the situation along the line of actual control (LAC), with the former underlining that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the development of bilateral relations.

The Indian side also reiterated the need for early convening of the next meeting of the Expert Level Mechanism on trans-border rivers, which was established in 2006, and emphasised the importance of sharing technical details on upstream projects.

Following the recent announcement of a mega dam project by China, India has been raising the need for transparency and consultation with downstream countries on such upstream activities.

According to the Indian govt, as a lower riparian state with established user rights to the waters of trans-border rivers, India routinely conveys its views and concerns to the Chinese authorities, and has urged them to ensure that the interests of downstream states are not harmed by activities in upstream areas. India has repeatedly stressed resumption of the provision of hydrological data and other cooperation pertaining to trans-border rivers.





The 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation & Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC) on Thursday saw both sides agreeing to continue using existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander-level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC.

World.title: ‘Little hope of tracing 2 missing sailors’, Centre informs Supreme Court
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The government informed the Supreme Court on Friday that there is very little hope of locating two Indian seafarers who are missing since the drone attack on Palau-flagged merchant ship M V AGN Ragnar on July 25 while it was departing Ukrainian waters.

Filing a combined action-taken report by MEA and the Directorate General of Maritime Administration, solicitor general (SG) Tushar Mehta told the bench that despite intense search and rescue operations, the missing Indian seafarers â Deepak Kumar Gupta and Ram Chandra Dubey â could not be located.

The Supreme Court told Mehta to facilitate the familiesâ availing maritime insurance payments.

World.title: Political parties urge govt. to convene all-party meeting on Mekedatu project
World.content:
Leaders of several political parties in Tamil Nadu on Friday urged the State government to convene an all-party meeting on the proposed Mekedatu dam project in Karnataka, saying a united political and legal response was essential to protect the State’s share of Cauvery water.

Speaking at a demonstration organised by Puthiya Tamilagam in Chennai, the leaders accused successive governments in Karnataka of failing to release Tamil Nadu’s due share of Cauvery water in accordance with tribunal and Supreme Court orders.

They contended that the State had often received only surplus water released during periods of heavy rainfall rather than its allocated share.

Naam Tamilar Katchi chief co-ordinator Seeman alleged that Karnataka had repeatedly failed to comply with Cauvery water-sharing orders. He said the State should insist on receiving its legally allocated 177.25 tmcft of water. He alleged that successive governments at the Centre had failed to safeguard Tamil Nadu’s interests and urged the State government to pursue all available political and legal measures to secure the State’s rightful share of Cauvery water.

Puthiya Tamilagam founder K. Krishnasamy said the proposed Mekedatu dam would further reduce flows to Tamil Nadu if constructed. He claimed Karnataka had failed to release the quantity of water due to Tamil Nadu, affecting kuruvai cultivation this season in the Delta districts.

Mr. Krishnasamy also criticised the State government for not initiating stronger legal action to secure the release of water.

Tamilaga Vaazhvurimai Katchi president T. Velmurugan called on political parties in Tamil Nadu to unite on the Mekedatu issue, including during the upcoming byelection.

Representatives of the Pattali Makkal Katchi, Indiya Jananayaga Katchi, and other parties, also participated.

World.title: GCC sets August-end as deadline for pre-monsoon preparedness work
World.content:
The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) plans to complete pending works and bridge gaps in the city’s storm-water drain (SWD) network by the end of August.

According to officials in the Storm Water Drain Department, the number of SWD network gaps was reduced to 87 from 115 since July 15, covering an estimated distance of 870 m.

On the civic body’s pre-monsoon preparedness, officials said tenders for cleaning silt catch pits across all zones had been finalised and work orders issued, with operations already under way. They added that the city’s waterbodies were also being rejuvenated, primarily through the deepening of ponds.

Officials said that efforts to remove structural encroachments remained stalled due to pending litigations in courts.

As for recurring sewer blockages, they attributed the problem to the 40-year-old sewerage pipeline infrastructure maintained by the Chennai Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (CMWSSB),and noted that it was currently unable to handle the city’s capacity demands.

The GCC plans to complete its comprehensive pre-monsoon preparedness works by August-end.

Currently, 68,281 of the total 1,09,975 silt catch pits have been cleaned.

Besides, of the 245 ponds maintained by the civic body across its 15 zones, improvement works have been sanctioned for 83 at an estimated cost of ₹214.02 crore. Restoration has been completed in 49 ponds, while work is under progress at 34 locations.

Infrastructure coordination remains an ongoing issue, with CMWSSB project delays resulting in unauthorised road cuts and dumping of excess soil at various work sites.

World.title: U.S. Senate passes Russia sanctions bill that seeks 100% tariffs on India, four others
World.content:
The U.S. Senate voted overwhelmingly to approve a bill to punish Russia and key buyers of its petroleum products, such as China and India, claiming that such trade helps fuel the Ukraine war.

The bill, renamed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, was approved by the Senate by an 86-11 vote.

It allows President Donald Trump to impose 100% tariffs on goods from countries that are the top five importers of Russian oil and gas.

At present China, India, Azerbaijan, Hungary and Slovakia are top five importers of oil and gas from Russia.

In addition to Russia sanctions, the bill would extend till 2031 the expiration date of the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996, which penalises companies that invest in Iran’s energy sector.

The bipartisan bill was championed by Republican senator Lindsey Graham, who passed away on July 11, and Democrat Richard Blumenthal.

After Graham’s sudden death following a trip to Kyiv, leaders across the aisle moved with renewed vigour to ensure passage of the bill and honour the late Senator’s legacy as an ally of Ukraine.

“This bill forces those primary countries keeping Russia’s economy afloat to make a simple yet critical choice – a choice between doing business with America or buying cheap Russian energy,” said Darline Graham, the late senator’s sister who was appointed to his seat after his death.

It also seeks to impose sanctions on Russian leaders and officials, targeting Russian President Vladimir Putin, oligarchs and financial institutions.

Following the vote, Senator Blumenthal told reporters that Lindsey Graham would be “proud of what we’ve done”.

“These sledgehammer sanctions and tariffs will stop all who are complicit in this murderous, criminal war of aggression against brave free people,” Mr. Blumenthal said.

Some Democrats have warned that the bill would give Mr. Trump new tariff powers at a time when he has put such levies at the centre of his trade policy.

The bill will now go to the House of Representatives for approval when it reconvenes on August 31.

Democrat Congressmen Gregory Meeks and Don Beyer have criticised the legislation for creating “sweeping new tariff authorities that the president could weaponise with abandon, as he has repeatedly done in the past”.

“We welcome our Senate colleagues’ urgent effort to support Ukraine and punish Russia for its continued illegal war, but this bill would not achieve those goals. Instead, it would allow President Trump to dodge holding Russia accountable and impose yet more tariffs in his destructive trade wars, leaving Americans to foot the bill,” the two leaders said.

World.title: Bihar cabinet gives nod to fill up 22,981 posts of Anganwadi workers
World.content:
The Bihar cabinet on Wednesday (July 29, 2026) gave its nod to fill up the 22,891 posts of Anganwadi Worker/Helper under the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) in the State.

It was among 24 decisions taken at today’s Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary.

The Cabinet approved “Anganwadi Worker/Helper Selection Guidelines- 2026”, which will initiate the process to fill the total 22,891 vacant posts, comprising 6,141 Anganwadi Workers and 16,750 Anganwadi Helpers, the Cabinet Secretariat Department’s Additional Chief Secretary (ACS) Arvind Kumar Chaudhary told reporters in a post-Cabinet briefing.

Under the ICDS scheme, children up to six years of age, pregnant women, lactating mothers, and other beneficiaries are provided with supplementary nutrition, pre-school education, health check-ups, referral services, immunisation, and nutrition & health education through Anganwadi Centres.

The Cabinet gave its nod for the creation of one post each of District and Additional Sessions Judge, totalling 19 (nineteen) posts, in the Exclusive Special Courts established for the speedy disposal of cases pending under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

The 19 posts will be filled in 19 judgeships, namely: West Champaran (Bettiah), Madhubani, Bhojpur (Ara), Siwan, Araria, Supaul, Khagaria, Jehanabad, Buxar, Jamui, Kaimur, Katihar, Sitamarhi, Munger, Madhepura, Banka, Sheikhpura, Aurangabad, and Lakhisarai.

Similarly, the Cabinet also decided to approve the creation of three (03) posts of District and Additional Sessions Judges for the establishment of two (02) additional Special Courts at Patna and one (01) additional Special Court at Muzaffarpur.

The Cabinet also gave its approval for the implementation of the e-Cabinet system in the State and the selection and award of work to the National Informatics Centre (NIC) on a nomination basis, Mr. Chaudhary said.

The State will establish a completely secure, digital technology-based paperless environment. This will lead to savings in administrative time, operational costs, and human effort, while also promoting a faster, more transparent, and workflow-based system of governance, he added.

In another important decision, the cabinet approved the Bihar Registration (Amendment) Rules, 2026, which will provide the facility of home registration for land, plots, and flats through the Mobile Registration Unit to senior citizens aged 75 years or above.

It may be noted that earlier, the Cabinet had provided the facility to senior citizens aged 80 years or above to register land, plots, or flats from the comfort of their homes but Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary while launching the paperless registration facility on July 11, 2026 had announced that the home registration facility for land, plots, and flats would be extended to senior citizens aged 75 years or above.

Under the Bihar State Vegetable Processing and Marketing Scheme, a scheme worth ₹106.39 crore has been approved for the strengthening and expansion of Vegfed’s three-tier cooperative structure.

Block-level basic infrastructure will be constructed, and arrangements for working capital for cooperative societies and reefer vehicles will be developed.

It also gave its administrative approval for the Road Construction Department’s proposal for two high-level RCC bridge construction projects on NH-333A in Jamui district. The construction of a new bridge at Nariyana Ghat over Kiul River will be built at the 72nd km on Khaira-Sono Road for ₹93.82 crore. The construction of a new bridge at Mangobandar over Suknar River at the 80th km of Khaira-Sono Road for ₹55.96 crore.

Meanwhile, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced that the Education Department has sent the requisition to the Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) for the appointment of 32,388 teachers under TRE-4.

World.title: Kerala Tourism to push for driver facilities in star-rating norms for hotels and resorts
World.content:
Kerala Tourism (KT) will take up with the Centre the need to include amenities such as well-maintained washrooms and dormitories in the checklist used by the Union Tourism Ministry to issue star ratings to hotels and resorts, a senior KT official said.

This comes in the wake of a protest by drivers on Friday at a luxury hotel here, seeking properly maintained washrooms for their use.

“At present, dedicated amenities for drivers are not mandatory for hotels and resorts to obtain classification from the Central agency. Rather, the focus is on fulfilling all the mandatory criteria with regard to hosting guests who visit them for accommodation or for food. Despite this, KT and Kerala Travel Mart [KTM] Society attempted to create such infrastructure at hotels and resorts a few years ago. But much more needs to be done,” the official said.

In the absence of such amenities yet to be made part of the classification process, there are two options. One is to construct them in properties where land is available, while the other is for them to tie up with lodges or with budget hotels nearby, where drivers can stay at affordable rates, he added.

Sources in the Union Tourism Ministry confirmed that they are focussed exclusively on the infrastructure available to maximise the ‘guest experience’ at hotels and resorts. “However, local bodies have the power to insist on restrooms and other infrastructure for drivers since they issue the no-objection certificate [NOC] for such units to commence operations.”

Back in September 2024, the Kerala government had issued an order making it mandatory for tourist accommodation units to provide clean and adequate restroom facilities for tourist taxi drivers, considering the vital role they played in the tourism industry. The order was issued after then Tourism Minister convened a stakeholder meeting to discuss issues faced by drivers of tourist vehicles.

Citing the need to enforce the order, Jackson Varghese, who led a hunger strike in 2019 demanding the rights of online taxi drivers, and who served as State president of the Kerala Online Drivers’ Union, said the Government Order was binding on all four- and five-star accommodation units in Kerala. They ought to provide clean dormitory accommodation and basic infrastructure for drivers who brought or picked up guests. “With many such units not implementing the order, drivers are often forced to use washrooms in nearby shopping malls or eateries. They also have no other option but to sleep inside their cars.”

Over the past 10 years, several drivers have died after sleeping inside their cars with the air conditioning running, he said, citing cases where fuel ran out and drivers were exposed to carbon monoxide and other exhaust fumes. The situation is grave in Alappuzha, where drivers sleep beneath trees or by the roadside, after dropping off their guests who stay in houseboats, he said.

World.title: Workshop to draft action plans for welfare of SHGs begins in Kochi
World.content:
A southern-level workshop as part of the National Supportive Supervision Framework (NSSF) under the Ministry of Rural Development to nurture cluster-level federations began here on Wednesday.

The event was part of drafting new action plans to ensure the social and financial welfare of self-help groups and members of neighbourhood groups. Jui Bhattacharya, national mission manager for the National Mission Management Unit, inaugurated the workshop. The aim is to make each cluster-level federation financially self-sustaining by 2047, she was quoted as saying in a release issued here.

Representatives from Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry, and Lakshadweep shared their suggestions and participated in group discussions on the occasion.

An action plan to suit the requirements of each State will be prepared after taking into consideration various factors like human resources, financial sustainability, and benefits for the members, according to the release.

World.title: AKPCTA seeks govt. intervention to end administrative crisis at technical varsity
World.content:
The State committee of the All Kerala Private College Teachers Association (AKPCTA) has urged the Kerala government to intervene immediately to resolve the administrative crisis at A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technological University, alleging that the Vice-Chancellor’s actions have paralysed the functioning of the varsity.

The association demanded that a Syndicate meeting be convened without further delay to approve pending appointments and promotions.

In a press statement, AKPCTA general secretary A. Nishanth said the Syndicate had not met for the past five months, despite the varsity statute requiring meetings at least once every two months. As a result, the approval of appointments of more than 30 employees ranging from office assistants to Assistant Professors at three engineering colleges has been delayed. The association said the employees, including those with disabilities, had been working for nearly two years without receiving salaries due to lack of approval.

The association also alleged that the promotion files of around 270 teachers and over 40 office staff remained pending. Although the files were placed before previous Syndicate meetings, they were repeatedly deferred on technical grounds, citing non-consideration by standing committees.

Mr. Nishanth said the standing committee was constituted at the Syndicate meeting held in February, but the minutes of the meeting were later withdrawn due to technical issues, with only the Budget being recorded as approved. Since then, no Syndicate meeting has been convened, the AKPCTA said.

The teachers’ body further raised concerns over the decision to sanction new courses this year without inspecting the infrastructure of colleges. It alleged that the move had triggered several complaints and questioned whether officials who had earlier faced inquiries over granting courses before university statutes came into force and approving courses for institutions without affiliations were behind the latest decisions.

AKPCTA further accused Vice-Chancellor Ciza Thomas of allegedly using the special powers granted under the University Act for academic matters to take decisions on financial issues, which it termed unlawful. Unlike other varsities, the Technical university V-C has no independent financial powers, yet the university is functioning under one-person rule, the association alleged.

The association said several urgent decisions relating to the commencement of the new academic year had been delayed because of the administrative deadlock.

AKPCTA State president Sanjeev G.N. called on the State government to take immediate steps to resolve the crisis and ensure that the Syndicate meets at the earliest to approve all pending appointments and promotions.

Responding to the association’s claims that the absence of Syndicate meetings had delayed placements and promotions, the Vice-Chancellor said appointments are made by colleges, while placements under the career advancement scheme required detailed scrutiny by a Syndicate sub-committee.

She said the process would be taken up at the Syndicate meeting scheduled this week. She also denied allegations of approving new courses without inspection, clarifying that only provisional approval, subject to inspection, had been granted.

Defending the financial decisions, she said the emergency powers under Clause 14(5) of the University Act permitted such actions, subject to the Syndicate’s ratification.

She also dismissed allegations of outsourcing an online constitution course, saying no private agency had been engaged, and that the proposal had been deferred.

She said spreading baseless allegations could undermine students’ confidence in the university.

World.title: Bangladeshi national arrested in Kozhikode over illegal stay
World.content:
​The Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) arrested a Bangladeshi national, identified as Muhammad Hassan, from Mavoor here on Wednesday.

Police sources said Hassan was apprehended during an inspection at a rented house following a tip-off.

​During the search, the ATS team recovered his Bangladeshi identity documents and currency. Hassan and his friend had moved into the house just a day earlier. On seeing the ATS team, the person accompanying him reportedly fled the scene. ​The police have intensified search for him.

The ATS also received information that another friend of Hassan was staying in the same house, and efforts are on to trace him as well.

Meanwhile, Hassan was shifted to the Mavoor police station, and a case will be registered against him under the Immigration and Foreigners Act.

World.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye sign tripartite defence agreement in Makkah
World.content:
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Friday signed a joint defence pact in Makkah that empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, which seeks to strengthen the collective security of the three states, was signed by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince and PM Mohammad bin Salman, and Türkiye’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the “Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence” held at Al-Safa Palace.

The three countries announced the signing of the agreement in a joint statement published by the Foreign Office (FO) and Saudi Arabia’s official SPA press agency.

The statement said the pact reflected the three countries’ “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond, in pursuit of a secure and prosperous future”.

“The agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression, and stipulates that any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all.”

It also “provides for the enhancement of all aspects of defence cooperation” among the three countries, the statement added.

The agreement is “guided by the longstanding historical ties among the three states, based on the enduring bonds of brotherhood and Islamic solidarity that unite them, and building upon their shared strategic interests and longstanding defence cooperation”.

During the Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence, the “distinguished relations” between the three countries were reviewed, “along with a number of issues of mutual interest”, the statement noted.

Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif were also present at the signing ceremony.

The defence and foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Turkiye were in attendance as well, pictures showed.

Sealing the agreement in Makkah, the holiest site in Islam, adds symbolic heft to a pact that builds on longstanding bilateral military ties among the three countries.

The agreement ties together Pakistan, the only nuclear-armed Muslim country; Saudi Arabia, the home to Islam’s holiest sites and one of the world’s top oil exporters; and Turkiye, Nato’s second-largest military.

‘Shield of peace’

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif described the signing of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement as a “historic pact”, saying the three countries were united by faith, friendship and a shared commitment to peace and security.

In a post on X, the prime minister said he was honoured to sign the agreement alongside the Saudi crown prince and the Turkish president.

He said the pact would serve as a “shield of peace” for generations and expressed hope that it would bring prosperity to the three countries and the wider Muslim world. Shehbaz also appreciated Field Marshal Asim Munir’s efforts and dedication towards the agreement.

‘Historic day for Pakistan’

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, while talking to a private TV channel, described the signing of the joint defence agreement between the three states as a “historic day” for Pakistan, saying the pact reflected growing recognition of the country’s defence capabilities and strengthened ties among the three nations.

Speaking about the agreement, Tarar said the defence cooperation framework would take relations between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye to a new level. He credited Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir with bringing the three countries together, saying they had an “ideal working relationship” and that their teamwork had contributed to recent successes.

Tarar said the agreement was aimed at strengthening defence cooperation and served as a form of deterrence rather than aggression. The minister further said Pakistan’s capabilities had been demonstrated during last year’s conflict with India and claimed that the country had since played a role in promoting regional peace.

Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan said that the signing of the joint defence agreement by the crown prince, the president of Türkiye and the prime minister of Pakistan underscored the depth of the fraternal and strategic relations between the three countries.

He said the agreement marked an important milestone in their defence cooperation and reflected their shared desire to coordinate efforts to address challenges and threats affecting regional security and stability. He added that the pact embodied the three countries’ shared political will to safeguard security, support a more secure regional environment and pave the way for greater development and prosperity.

Saudi Arabia’s Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said the agreement “does not represent an effort to establish a military axis or a sectarian bloc”.

“Nor is it linked to any nuclear ambitions or arms race; rather, it is focused on building sustainable capabilities,” he wrote on X.

He noted that the deal “does not constitute a threat to the security of any country in the region, nor does it represent an escalation of tensions between any two states”.

The Saudi official further said the agreement “does not supersede or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between these countries”.

Mansoor Ahmed, of the Australian National University’s Strategic and Defence Studies Centre, said Islamabad and Ankara bring strong defence industries to the table, while Riyadh could contribute with technological spending.

While the pact comes in the backdrop of the US-Israel war on Iran, Bloomberg had reported in January — before the conflict began — that Ankara was seeking to join a separate mutual defence pact between Islamabad and Riyadh.

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both.

In January, Reuters quoted Defence Production Minister Raza Hayat Harraj as saying that a draft had been prepared after 10 months of talks. Turkish FM Hakan Fidan had said Ankara favoured an “inclusive platform that creates wider, bigger cooperation and stability”.

Pakistan has also sought to mediate efforts to end the US-Iran war, while Turkiye has played a diplomatic role in negotiations aimed at ending the war in Gaza.

The three countries, along with Egypt, have been closely involved in efforts to promote regional stability and contain the regional upheaval sparked by the US-Iran war.

The regional conflagration has rained missile fire onto Gulf oil exporters, with Iran targeting Gulf countries in retaliation for attacks carried out against it using US military bases in the region.

The deal also comes as a 2022 truce between Riyadh and the Houthi rebels in Yemen has broken down.

After the two sides traded fire for the first time in years last month, Houthis declared a maritime blockade against the kingdom, threatening access to its ports, and has claimed to have attacked Saudi tankers in the Red Sea.

Pakistan had condemned the Houthis’ threats to Saudi Arabia and to trading with the kingdom via the Red Sea. It also warned that it had the right to self-defence if its “maritime interests” were targeted in “any hostile act”.

As the conflict expanded onto new fronts, Saudi Arabia last week unveiled plans for a multinational maritime defence coalition to protect shipping and energy supply routes in the Red Sea. Fourteen countries, including Pakistan, have voiced support for the coalition.

Saudi crown prince meets PM Shehbaz, Erdogan

Crown Prince Salman held separate meetings with PM Shehbaz and President Erdogan at the Al-Safa Palace earlier in the day.

DPM Dar, CDF Munir and Asif were also present in the meeting with PM Shehbaz, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said.

Meanwhile, Erdogan’s office confirmed on X that he also held a meeting with Crown Prince Salman.

PM Shehbaz arrived in Saudi Arabia on a three-day visit on Thursday, while the Turkish president undertook a one-day visit today, Anadolu Agency reported.

Erdogan landed at King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah, from where he departed for Makkah by road, the Turkish news outlet reported.

PM Shehbaz had landed in Jeddah on Thursday. CDF Munir later joined the Pakistani delegation, which also included Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and Special Assistant to PM Tariq Fatemi.

On Friday morning, the delegation visited the Holy Kaaba and performed Umrah, the PMO said. PM Shehbaz is also expected to visit Masjid-i-Nabvi (PBUH) in Madina.

According to an earlier statement by the FO, discussions between the two sides were to “focus on consolidating the Pakistan-Saudi bilateral relations as well as exchange of views on regional and international developments of mutual interests”.

The FO had noted that although the visit was taking place amid heightened tensions in the Gulf, it carries “significance beyond the immediate crises and short-term considerations”.

It said the visit will “further strengthen bilateral relations, deepen strategic cooperation, enhance coordination on regional and international issues of mutual interest, and reinforce multilateral cooperation”.

“The visit marks Pakistan’s long-standing partnership with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia anchored in decades of mutual trust, cooperation and brotherhood,” the FO had emphasised.

Pakistan has provided training and technical assistance to Saudi forces for decades, while Turkiye and Pakistan have exchanged warships and training aircraft.

In 2023, Riyadh agreed to buy Turkish drones in what Ankara called its largest defence export contract. In April this year, Saudi Arabia said it received a military force and fighter jets from Pakistan to boost the kingdom’s security.

Additional input from AFP and Reuters

World.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs2.20, high-speed diesel by Rs1.50
World.content:
The government on Friday reduced the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.20 and Rs1.50 per litre, respectively.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs327.62 per litre while HSD will cost Rs380.86 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on HSD.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will apply from August 8 to 10.

The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Goods transporters to go on strike from Saturday after talks with govt fail
World.content:
Goods transporters and oil tanker operators began suspending their services on Friday night after negotiations with the government failed, ahead of their nationwide wheel-jam strike scheduled for Saturday.

All Pakistan Goods Transport Itehad spokesman and All Pakistan Goods Transport Owners Association President Mohammad Owais Chaudhry Advocate told Dawn that talks with Federal Minister for Communications Aleem Khan and other government officials had failed.

He said the negotiations ended without a breakthrough, prompting transporters, including edible oil tanker operators, petroleum oil tanker operators, truckers, trailer operators and other intercity transporters, to proceed with their previously announced strike.

“We have informed the government side about the problems we are facing and our concerns,” Chaudhry said, adding that the strike would continue until their demands were accepted.

However, the minister has assured the transporters that he would discuss their demands, and the next round of talks would be held on Monday morning.

The unified body of transporters had already announced that it would begin its wheel-jam strike from August 8, and warned that it would not be a token strike but an indefinite one.

“Commercial goods carriers across the country have already been taken off the roads and will remain stationed at designated places during the protest period,” Chaudhry said.

Among the key demands of the transporters is the uniform enforcement of axle-load limits across the country and permission for 10-wheel vehicles to carry up to 35 tonnes.

They have also demanded reductions in diesel prices and toll taxes, besides seeking relief in withholding tax to ease the financial burden on the transport sector.

The transporters have also called for the withdrawal of customs provisions that, according to the association, allow authorities to confiscate vehicles carrying goods found to be in violation of customs laws.

Other demands include the withdrawal of the Punjab Highway Patrol’s powers to issue challans to commercial vehicles, an end to what the association described as unnecessary challans and excessive fines on motorways and highways, and measures to facilitate the issuance of heavy transport vehicle licences to drivers.

World.title: Sindh govt constitutes third medical board for exhumation of Mir Ali Raza’s body
World.content:
After withdrawing its two earlier notifications, the Sindh government on Friday notified a newly constituted eight-member medical board to carry out the exhumation of 25-year-old business owner Mir Ali Raza’s body on Saturday.

The exhumation, which was originally scheduled for Friday, was deferred after the deceased’s family objected to the abrupt reconstitution of the medical board, just hours after the notification of the first one.

A notification issued by the Sindh Health Department on Friday named police surgeon Dr Sumaiyya Syed as the convener of the board and Dow University of Health Sciences (DUHS) Pathology Department head Professor Dr Naseem Ahmed as the pathologist.

The eight-member board also includes Jinnah Sindh Medical University’s (JSMU) Dr Farah Waseem as a forensic expert, Shanakht Project’s Amir Hassan Khan as a forensic identification expert, Additional Police Surgeon Dr Srichand, Jinnah Post-Graduate Medical Centre (JPMC) medicolegal officers Dr Kamran Khan and Dr Daniyal Mirza, and Office of Police Surgeon Administrative In-charge Dr Muhammad.

According to the notification, the board may also co-opt any expert member if required.

Moreover, a notification issued by the Office of the Police Surgeon said that the exhumation of Ali’s body would be carried out on Saturday, August 8, at 11am. A civil judge and judicial magistrate Karachi-XXI would also be present, according to the police surgeon’s office.

Reconstitution of board

On Thursday, a Karachi court allowed the exhumation of Ali’s body on an application filed by the victim’s father, directing the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medico-legal board for the exhumation of Ali’s body “at the earliest possible date and time”.

The court ruling came after a controversy emerged between the Karachi police surgeon and investigators over alleged loopholes in the medico-legal report regarding the post-mortem examination.

The Sindh Health Department then constituted the eight-member board, with the police surgeon as the convener. Dr Ahmed of Dow DUHS, Dr Waseem of JSMU, Amir Khan of Citizens Police Liaison Committee, Dr Sirichand, Dr Kamran and Dr Daniyal of JPCM and Dr Yaseen, the admin in-charge of the police surgeon’s office, were the other members of the board.

However, a new order had been issued by the Sindh Health Directorate. The notification said that the board had been reconstituted to conduct the exhumation and medico-legal examination of the deceased.

While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new board, its members were changed to Prof Dr Zakiuddin from DUHS, Prof Dr Kazi Akbar and Prof Dr Abid Hussain Chang from Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences and Hyderabad Police Surgeon Dr Waseem Khan.

Controversy over autopsy

Raza, owner of eatery Wafflix, had gone missing on July 28. The 25-year-old’s body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Gulistan-i-Jauhar.

Initially, on the complaint lodged by his father, a case was registered at the Ferozabad police station under Section 365 (kidnapping or abducting with intent secretly and wrongfully to confine a person) of the Pakistan Penal Code.

Police maintain that the investigation has revealed that Ali had been facing financial difficulties and had asked his friends for money the night he died.

According to police, he had left his home in PECHS Block-2 and hired a taxi through an app. The taxi driver dropped him a short distance from the spot where his body was found, police said.

The case took a new turn when Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed told a private news channel on Tuesday that the postmortem findings of Ali’s body had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs.

She said the reported entry wound, bullet trajectory and exit wound did not correspond with one another. While it was scientifically possible for a bullet to enter through the back and exit from the front, she stressed that her assessment was based only on the postmortem report and photographs, as she had not examined the body herself.

The police surgeon noted that entry wounds were typically smaller than exit wounds in firearm cases. She also said that gunshot residue, commonly found on the hands in suspected suicides, was not tested for in this case.

Her interview prompted the police authorities to issue a statement, terming such observations as having the potential to adversely affect the ongoing investigation.

The statement, however, said that exhumation of the dead body could be done on the medical board’s recommendation for further clarification by a committee of medico-legal experts with the court’s permission.

World.title: Bilawal claims 'certain elements' within PML-N are sowing division among allies, undermining PM Shehbaz
World.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari claimed on Friday that certain elements within the ruling PML-N were undermining Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and sowing discord between him and his political allies.

The PPP and the PML-N have been engaged in a war of words since the latter emerged in the lead in Mirpur polls on July 27. The PML-N has also won the majority of the seats in the second phase , with the PPP accusing it of rigging and other violent tactics in both phases.

The PPP chief was addressing an election rally in Azad Jammu and Kashmir’s Poonch district, where the third phase of elections in the region is slated to be held.

“High-profile people are saying that the government has collapsed. I’m not saying that, nor am I casting doubt on the prime minister’s intentions. He’s a good man with good intentions. But what can he do when the people around him have bad intentions?” Bilawal asked.

In reference to remarks he made earlier this week, the party chief highlighted that the PPP did not start the “countdown” to the government’s collapse, but rather these elements within the ruling party.

“The PML-N’s fight is not with the PPP — it happens in elections, as it has before. The real fight is entirely different, because the PM, with his good intentions and actions, is undermined by a large part of the PML-N,” Bilawal alleged.

“A big part of the PML-N wants the PM to fight not only the opposition, but also his own allies.”

He then asked the audience: “Have there ever been elections held in six phases in Kashmir’s history? If Kashmir is one, then the election should have been held on a single day.”

Bilawal said the elections were being held in phases “so that there is calm and the elections are peaceful, free and fair”, before asking: “But in which phase were the elections free, fair or peaceful?”

“In truth, elections were carried out in phases so they could rig them. They knew that 10 seats were in their pocket from the start,” he alleged.

“With the 10 seats in their pocket, they robbed Mirpur, they robbed Muzaffarabad, and they’re looking at you, in Poonch. They are looking at Bagh. On August 10, they will find out that those in Poonch and Bagh hunt tigers.”

Elections are being held across AJK in three phases . Polls in Mirpur and Muzaffarabad divisions were held on July 27 and August 2, respectively.

The first phase of polling in Mirpur saw the PML-N secure nine of the 13 seats while the PPP won the remaining four.

In the second phase in Muzaffarabad, the PML-N bagged 15 more seats, while the PPP managed to add just six more to its tally.

The third phase in Poonch division was set for August 10. Poonch Division comprises 11 constituencies — three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch and two in Sudhnoti district.

However, earlier today, the AJK Election Commission revised the schedule for the third phase of elections in the region, saying polling would only be held in Poonch Division’s Bagh and Haveli districts on August 10 amid concerns over the law and order situation.

The electoral process in the constituencies of Poonch district and Sudhnoti’s Pallandri would not be held on August 10, the Election Commission said, adding that it reviewed the “current situation” regarding the scheduled elections in Poonch.

It noted that according to a report it received from the AJK home secretary, there were “concerns over the law and order situation in some areas of Poonch district and Pallandri district”.

The commission’s decision comes in the wake of clashes that took place between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Poonch district’s Rawalakot on July 27, which reportedly resulted in several casualties.

Rawalakot has been gripped by unrest since early June , with the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) staging sit-ins periodically.

The JAAC, which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now.

World.title: SCBA backs call for new provinces, calls it 'step forward' for better governance
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) — a premier lawyers’ body — on Friday voiced support for the controversial proposal recently put forward by Interior Minister Syed Mohsin Naqvi regarding the creation of new provinces in the country.

Recently, while addressing the Pakistan Economic Summit 2026, the interior minister had urged all political parties to resolve various national issues, including the question of creating new provinces. He termed this the only solution to improving the country’s overall condition, which he said had “collapsed”.

Speaking at the Full Court Reference held at the Supreme Court (SC) in honour of Justice Musarrat Hilali on the occasion of her laying down her judicial robes, SCBA President Haroonur Rashid said the association endorsed and supported the suggestion to create new provinces.

Headed by Chief Justice of Pakistan (CJP) Yahya Afridi, the reference was attended by SC judges both in person and via video link.

The reference was also attended by Additional Attorney General (AAG) Chaudhry Aamir Rehman, representatives of the SCBA and the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC), senior members of the legal fraternity, court officers, media representatives and others.

“The association believes that any constitutional measure for the creation of more provinces would be a step forward towards an enhanced governance system through devolved and equitable administration at the grassroots level, the creation of equal opportunities for parallel economic development, and stronger political stability in the country,” the SCBA president said.

He added that the creation of more provinces would also improve the standard of living by addressing the economic challenges faced by the people of the country.

Meanwhile, in its 250th meeting held in Islamabad on Friday, the PBC — the apex body of the legal fraternity — said it firmly believed that all constitutional matters must be addressed strictly within the framework of the Constitution.

The PBC deliberated upon the issue of the creation of new administrative units and provinces in the country. It reaffirmed through a resolution that the legal fraternity was committed to upholding the Constitution, and that members were of the unanimous view that the question of creating new provinces should be considered in accordance with the constitutional principles and procedures.

The resolution emphasised that all political parties, irrespective of their political differences, should act in the “larger national interest” and initiate a “comprehensive and meaningful dialogue” for the betterment of the country and its people.

The PBC resolved that, if the establishment of new provinces was deemed necessary, it must be carried out strictly in accordance with the Constitution through due parliamentary process and national consensus.
